title: Reju targets industrial-scale production of recycled knitted fabrics
title_ko: Reju는 재활용 편직물의 산업 규모 생산을 목표로 하고 있습니다.
summary: Recycled polyester specialist Reju has partnered with a group of circular knitting mills to expand the industrial-scale production of post-consumer textile-to-textile recycled fabrics. Figure: Access...
content: Recycled polyester specialist Reju has partnered with a group of circular knitting mills to expand the industrial-scale production of post-consumer textile-to-textile recycled fabrics. Figure: Access to high-volume jersey production and certified dyeing and finishing processes will support the development of recycled fabrics for wider textile applications. The partnerships will give Reju access to different circular knitting and fabric manufacturing processes. These include circular knit design, chain-of-custody verified recycling, high-volume jersey production, and sustainability-certified dyeing and finishing. The collaboration aims to connect recycled polyester production with the capabilities needed to manufacture finished fabrics at commercial scale. It will help Reju move regenerated polyester from recycled raw materials to market-ready knitted fabrics. Access to high-volume jersey production and certified dyeing and finishing processes will support the development of recycled fabrics for wider textile applications. The partnerships also highlight the importance of cooperation between recycling companies and textile mills in building a textile-to-textile recycling supply chain. Scaling recycled polyester into finished fabrics requires not only recycling technology but also access to established knitting, dyeing, and finishing facilities. Reju's approach focuses on expanding the use of post-consumer textile waste as a feedstock for new polyester fabrics.

summary: At ITMA ASIA 2026, KARL MAYER will demonstrate its expertise in processing staple fibers during warp preparation and will return to where this technology belongs: the Weaving Hall, at Booth 3/A24. The focus here will be on the latest-generation WARPDIRECT direct warping machine, featuring various yarn tensioners, as well as the sophisticated HSB Size Box […] The post Weaving Hall of ITMA ASIA 2026: High-Performance Warp Preparation for High-Quality Fabrics Made from Staple Fibers and New Horizons in Textiles appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: At ITMA ASIA 2026, KARL MAYER will demonstrate its expertise in processing staple fibers during warp preparation and will return to where this technology belongs: the Weaving Hall, at Booth 3/A24 . The focus here will be on the latest-generation WARPDIRECT direct warping machine, featuring various yarn tensioners, as well as the sophisticated HSB Size Box – the centerpiece of the innovative PROSIZE sizing machine. Both technologies are aimed specifically at manufacturers of high-quality goods in the commodity sector. „Our machines produce warp beams of the highest quality with high process efficiency. This offers particular advantages to textile manufacturers who are focused on generating real added value in a highly competitive market,“ says Enzo Paoli, President of the Warp Preparation Business Unit at KARL MAYER. WARPDIRECT: With the highest speed to precision warp beams Since its launch at the end of last year, the WARPDIRECT 2.0 has already been successfully deployed worldwide. Its performance is particularly valued in India, but also in China and Europe. Its strengths include identical warping lengths for all warp beams and high production output. In practice, warping speeds of up to 1,200 m/min are achieved. In addition, the current machine version stands out thanks to an upgrade to the press roll system. The change from hydraulic to electric operation reduces maintenance requirements while ensuring precise warping quality. In combination with an optimal yarn depositing device, this results in completely cylindrical beams with precise yarn arrangement. Sampaio, RDD Textiles, Tintex Textiles, FOV Fabrics, Utenos Trikotažas and Swisstex Direct […] The post Reju expands textile mill network appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Reju is working with six textile mills in Europe and the Americas to develop finished fabrics from regenerated polyester, as it prepares to establish an international network of industrial-scale textile recycling facilities. The Paris-based company, owned by Technip Energies, is collaborating with A. Sampaio, RDD Textiles, Tintex Textiles, FOV Fabrics, Utenos Trikotažas and Swisstex Direct to demonstrate how polyester recovered from post-consumer textile waste can be incorporated into commercially viable fabrics. These partnerships represent an important step in connecting Reju’s planned recycling operations with downstream textile manufacturing. Reju is developing a chemical recycling process based on technology originating from IBM Research, with the aim of recovering polyester from discarded textiles and returning it to the textile supply chain without the quality limitations associated with conventional mechanical recycling. The company is currently progressing plans for a network of Regeneration Hubs capable of processing post-consumer polyester waste at industrial scale. Establishing recycling capacity, however, is only one part of the challenge – ensuring regenerated materials can be processed efficiently by existing textile manufacturers and meet the performance requirements of brands is equally important. The six participating mills will provide a range of complementary manufacturing capabilities. In Portugal, A. Sampaio contributes more than 75 years of experience in circular knitted fabrics, while RDD Textiles specialises in other knitted constructions, recycled and bio-based materials and advanced dyeing technologies. The partnership brings together the voice of European textile and clothing manufacturing and a leading global convener of the fashion industry, with a shared ambition for a thriving, sustainable and competitive European textile and clothing industry. Through the alliance, the two organisations will align their European and global policy agendas as closely as possible and coordinate supportive activities to promote sustainability effectively and efficiently across the textile and clothing value chain. The collaboration rests on a simple premise: each party brings unique capacity and capability, and together they can achieve more than either could alone. The partnership comes at a decisive moment. Shifting consumer expectations, new regulation, margin pressure, geopolitical turmoil and innovation are colliding with escalating crises in climate, biodiversity, water and resources. Together, these forces are rewriting the rules of the fashion industry, changing business models, production systems, materials and the flow of capital. Business must find a new model to navigate this complex environment. Regulation is now one of the most powerful drivers of change in this transition. The evolving legislative landscape brings both opportunity and complexity. title: Policy alignment is critical for green industrial transition
summary: The industrial shift toward lower emissions, cleaner energy and more resource-efficient production is accelerating. But the pace of that transition will depend on how well policy keeps up with market...
content: The industrial shift toward lower emissions, cleaner energy and more resource-efficient production is accelerating. But the pace of that transition will depend on how well policy keeps up with market reality. Bangladesh has raised its climate and energy ambition through its latest Nationally Determined Contribution, or NDC 3.0. At the same time, global brands are pushing suppliers toward renewable energy, recycled materials, lower emissions and more circular production systems. Courtesy: Collected For export-oriented industries, these are no longer separate sustainability issues. They are directly linked with cost, investment, market access and long-term competitiveness. Man-made fibre needs stronger policy support Globally, man-made fibres account for the larger share of textile fibre consumption. Bangladesh, however, remains heavily dependent on cotton. This matters because the global fashion industry is moving toward more synthetic, recycled and blended materials. Man-made fibres offer versatility, durability and, in many applications, stronger recycling potential. The issue is not about moving away from cotton. It is about reducing overdependence on one fibre base and building capacity in product categories where global demand is expanding. That requires investment across fibre production, spinning, weaving, knitting, fabric development and garment manufacturing. Policy has not always supported that transition. For years, manufacturers faced situations where some raw materials attracted higher duties than finished products. Although some of these issues have been addressed, the broader lesson remains. If policy discourages investment in emerging industrial capacity, the country loses time. This will become more important as Bangladesh moves beyond LDC trade preferen

content: The ZDHC Foundation today launched Version 4.0 of its ZDHC Manufacturing Restricted Substances List (ZDHC MRSL). This update reflects the latest scientific developments and evolving industry needs. The ZDHC Manufacturing Restricted Substances List provides a harmonized, science-based framework for restricting hazardous substances in chemical formulations used during manufacturing. Unlike traditional Restricted Substances Lists, which focus on finished products, the ZDHC MRSL addresses chemicals at their source, helping to prevent hazardous substances from entering production processes in the first place. ZDHC developed the update through its established MRSL governance process and had the ZDHC MRSL Council independently assess it, drawing on scientific, regulatory, and industry evidence as well as stakeholder review. Independent governance and MRSL CouncilThe updates in ZDHC MRSL V4.0 build on the ongoing review process led by the ZDHC MRSL Council, an independent group of technical experts representing diverse segments of the textile, apparel, leather and footwear industries, alongside other relevant stakeholders. The Council uses an objective, science-based approach to assess proposed substances and recommend their inclusion in the ZDHC MRSL or MRSL Candidate List. For Version 4.0, this assessment took into account developments in relevant regulatory lists, including Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) and Substances of Very High Concern (SVHC), as well as inputs from the ZDHC Chemical Watchlist. The proposed updates also underwent a stakeholder review to gather broader industry feedback. content: New York Fashion Innovation Center (NYFIC) has opened applications for the fifth and final scheduled round of its Sustainable Textile Innovation Grants, offering $10,000 per grant to support projects that advance sustainability in the textile and fashion industry. The funding opportunity is open to a wide range of applicants, including textile and fashion designers, sustainable fashion entrepreneurs, startups, researchers, innovators, businesses and organizations developing solutions for a more sustainable textile ecosystem. The grant program offers two funding tracks, General Topic Grants and Special Focus Grants, to support sustainable innovations across the textile and fashion industry. Eligible projects include innovative materials, sustainable production methods, and technologies that advance environmental and social sustainability throughout the fashion value chain. Applications will remain open until January 6, 2027, with award recipients expected to be announced in early Spring 2027. According to NYFIC, the grants are designed to help innovators transform promising ideas into practical solutions that can drive positive change within the global textile and apparel sector. In addition to the current funding round, NYFIC has announced plans to introduce Adaptive Fashion Innovation Grants in 2027. The initiative is expected to provide six grants of up to $10,000 each to support innovations that improve fashion accessibility, functionality and inclusivity for people with disabilities. Industry stakeholders view such funding programs as important catalysts for accelerating sustainable innovation, encouraging collaboration and supporting the development of next-generation textile technologies. content: Dishang Group has secured the State-of-the-Art Manufacturer title at the recent 2026 Professional Clothing Industry Association Worldwide (PCIAW) Awards, retaining the accolade for the second year running. Presented at the annual sector gathering in London, it honours Dishang’s continued capital investment in industrial technology, operational agility and greener production methods across its international network. Headquartered in Weihai, Shandong Province, China, Dishang Group operates more than 90 wholly owned manufacturing sites alongside 200 production partners globally, engineering end-to-end design and garment solutions for brands with products spanning menswear, womenswear, activewear, tailoring and workwear. The consecutive win reflects rapid developments across the business since last year. Over the past twelve months, Dishang has deepened the rollout of its Smart Digital Manufacturing Initiative, embedding machine learning, robotic handling and automated data monitoring into daily factory workflows. Other highlights from the past year that helped the company retain its title include the increased use of an AI-led energy platform that now watches over 80% of Dishang’s manufacturing facilities, helping shave 12% off per-unit energy consumption compared with 2024 levels. On the factory floor, high-speed 3D digital sampling and AI-driven design tools and textile-to-textile recycling technologies continue to help reduce the environmental impact of garment production, meeting the growing retail demand for demonstrable, audited supply-chain credentials. From its UK design headquarters at The Chapel in Harrogate, Dishang (UK) acts as the direct technical and commercial channel between British and European clothing brands and the group’s far-reaching factory base. The CHT Group is proud that the jury has […] The post CHT Germany GmbH is a finalist for the “German Sustainability Award Companies 2027” appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Jury recognizes the CHT Group’s efforts to advance sustainable transformation and its integration of chemical product development with industrial customer processes CHT Germany GmbH, part of the foundation-owned CHT Group, is a finalist for the “German Sustainability Award Companies 2027” in the Large Companies size class. The CHT Group is proud that the jury has selected the company for this prestigious award. The finalist recognition honors the CHT Group’s extensive efforts to advance sustainable transformation across product development and industrial applications. The jury was particularly impressed by the integration of chemical product development with industrial customer processes. It highlights the PIGMENTURA textile dyeing process using a pad-dry process as an approach to reducing water consumption. The jury also recognizes the CHT Group’s work on product carbon footprints and its systematic assessment of critical substances. Within the CHT Group, a calculation tool supports assessing product carbon footprints as early as the product development stage. In addition, a science-based internal classification system helps identify critical substances and replace them wherever technically and economically feasible. In this way, the CHT Group incorporates key sustainability considerations from the development stage onward, connecting process design, transparency, and substance selection with the requirements of industrial applications. The company is a finalist for the German Sustainability Award Companies. title: UK could unlock more than £93 billion and 550,000 new jobs if we take bolder steps towards a circular economy
summary: · POWERING GOOD GROWTH – new report details jobs, business opportunities and local growth across the UK through the circular economy· Circular economy jobs increased in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland between 2019 and 2024, while England saw a modest decline A new report from global environmental action NGO WRAP shows the scale of opportunities […] The post UK could unlock more than £93 billion and 550,000 new jobs if we take bolder steps towards a circular economy appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: · POWERING GOOD GROWTH – new report details jobs, business opportunities and local growth across the UK through the circular economy · Circular economy jobs increased in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland between 2019 and 2024, while England saw a modest decline A new report from global environmental action NGO WRAP shows the scale of opportunities for businesses and jobs across the UK through greater adoption of the ‘Circular Economy’ and calculates the untapped financial benefits in activities ranging from recycling, repair, reuse, second-hand retail, to rental and leasing business models. Published the day after Chancellor John Healey’s budget focussed on youth employment, apprenticeships and job creation through infrastructure and investment, WRAP’s report POWERING GOOD GROWTH – The Circular Economy Opportunity for Jobs, Manufacturing and Every Region of the UK illustrates how the UK could generate an additional £93 billion Gross Value Added (GVA) and support 550,000 new jobs, by taking bolder steps towards a circular economy. The findings suggest that circular economy activities such as repair, remanufacturing, reuse, recycling and biorefining can help spread economic opportunity across the UK by creating jobs in every nation and region, strengthening local supply chains and attracting investment into communities undergoing industrial transition. In 2024, the circular economy sectors supported almost 559,000 jobs across the UK, generating more than £53 billion in GVA. WRAP’s latest examination – updating its 2019 assessment – shows the circular economy continues to provide a substantial employment base, support domestic resource flows, and strengthen economic resilience. content: Dear Fellow Industry Owners and Colleagues, Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) industry remains one of the key pillars of the national economy, contributing significantly to foreign exchange earnings, employment generation, women’s economic empowerment, and industrial development. However, ensuring the industry’s long-term sustainability requires a balanced approach that addresses fair wages, employment generation, workforce skill development, productivity enhancement, and international competitiveness. Figure: Engineer Mohammad Aktaruzzaman, Former Chairman, BGMEA Standing Committee on Compliance, Managing Director, ENTRUST Group Increasing the minimum wage alone cannot guarantee workers’ long-term welfare. Sustainable employment opportunities, improved productivity, and the industry’s overall financial viability must also be secured. Drawing on my extensive experience in the garment industry and involvement in BGMEA’s compliance-related activities, I would like to present several observations and policy recommendations concerning Bangladesh’s existing minimum wage structure. These proposals are intended for consideration by BGMEA, BKMEA, relevant government authorities, international buyers and brands, and other industry stakeholders. 1. summary: Karl Mayer will introduce its new Multiply BX biaxial warp knitting machine during ITMA ASIA 2026, targeting the growing demand for high-performance reinforcement textiles used in wind turbine rotor blades. The machine, developed specifically for the wind power industry, will be demonstrated at the company’s manufacturing facility in Changzhou, China, during a Product Show coinciding […] The post New biaxial warp knitting machine for wind power applications appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Karl Mayer will introduce its new Multiply BX biaxial warp knitting machine during ITMA ASIA 2026, targeting the growing demand for high-performance reinforcement textiles used in wind turbine rotor blades. The machine, developed specifically for the wind power industry, will be demonstrated at the company’s manufacturing facility in Changzhou, China, during a Product Show coinciding with the international textile machinery exhibition in Shanghai. Designed for the efficient production of biaxial non-crimp fabrics, the Multiply BX processes glass fibres into reinforcement textiles with a high proportion of filler yarns, lightweight weft yarns and long stitch lengths. These structures are particularly suited to the longitudinal reinforcement requirements of modern wind turbine blades. According to Karl Mayer, the new machine delivers productivity improvements of 20-25% compared with its established Max Glass ECO model, achieving production speeds of 1,600-2,200 min⁻¹ and output of up to 500 metres per hour, depending on stitch length. The Multiply BX achieves its highest performance at stitch lengths of 4-5 mm, commonly used in wind power applications. It accommodates filler yarns of up to 2,400 tex alongside lightweight weft yarns of 100-200 tex, which provide transverse stabilisation while maintaining the emphasis on longitudinal reinforcement. The typical weight ratio of filler to weft yarns is 6:1. Dr Jürgen Tröltzsch, Product Specialist for Composite Machines at Karl Mayer Technical Textiles. © Karl Mayer “When developing the Multiply BX, we consistently focused on the needs of our wind power customers. title_ko: 차세대 기능성 섬유로 해초 탐구
summary: Norrøna, the Norwegian outdoor brand known for durable, premium outerwear, is partnering with Australian materials company Uluu to develop a new kind of performance fibre made mostly from seaweed. While most plant-based plastic alternatives are made exclusively from land crops, Uluu is one of the first to make a plastic alternative using seaweed. Together, the […] The post Exploring seaweed as the next performance fibre appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Norrøna, the Norwegian outdoor brand known for durable, premium outerwear, is partnering with Australian materials company Uluu to develop a new kind of performance fibre made mostly from seaweed. While most plant-based plastic alternatives are made exclusively from land crops, Uluu is one of the first to make a plastic alternative using seaweed. Together, the two companies are exploring the potential of seaweed-derived polymers as an alternative to fossil-based synthetics, advancing research into regenerative raw materials for the future of outdoor apparel. The goal is to develop fibres and fabrics tough enough for the outdoors and one day use them in Norrøna products. The work runs parallel to Norrøna’s support of Bellona’s efforts to restore Arctic kelp ecosystems impacted by sea urchin overgrazing along Norway’s northern coast. “Building the next generation of outdoor materials requires brands to get involved before every question has been answered,” says Jørgen Jørgensen, CEO and fourth-generation owner of Norrøna. “For nearly a century, Norrøna has developed products around the demands of the outdoors. We are now bringing that experience upstream, helping shape the fibre itself around what outdoor performance requires.” Unlike synthetic material that can shed tiny fibres during wear and washing that stay in the environment for a long time, Uluu’s material is designed to biodegrade, passing TUV marine and home biodegradable tests. The process starts with a low-impact raw material, since seaweed is harvested without farmland, minimum freshwater or fertilizer. Fermentation The process works much like a brewery, fermenting sugars from the seaweed in saltwater to create a natural material that can then be made into fibre. title: Santoni to showcase smart knitting technologies at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026
summary: Santoni China Group will showcase its latest knitting technologies and AI-assisted digital solutions at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai this month. The technologies will cover sportswear, underwear...
content: Santoni China Group will showcase its latest knitting technologies and AI-assisted digital solutions at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai this month. The technologies will cover sportswear, underwear, swimwear and mattress fabrics. Figure: Santoni to showcase smart knitting technologies at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026.Courtesy: Collected Under the theme “Machines Evolved · Intelligence Delivered,” the group will present machinery from its Santoni, Jingmei and Terrot brands. The display will combine knitting machines, textile applications, AI-based design and connected manufacturing solutions. A key feature will be the SWS 3D AI design platform. It will demonstrate how artificial intelligence can support 3D textile design and product development. The company will also present its latest AI-assisted digital development program. The exhibition will highlight the integration of knitting machinery with digital design and connected production systems. This reflects the growing role of AI and digital technologies in improving textile product development and manufacturing processes. The focus on circular and seamless knitting technologies also highlights opportunities for the industry to develop new textile structures and applications across different product segments.

title: Hierarchy to Heterarchy: A Crossroads for Textile & Apparel Transformation
summary: COVID-19 revealed a paradox in organizational life: even with half the mid-level workforce physically present and reduced office hours, many companies not only survived but thrived. This disruption exposed inefficiencies in traditional hierarchies – layers of reporting, redundant roles, and micromanagement – that often obstruct value creation rather than enable it. Instead of information crawling […] The post Hierarchy to Heterarchy: A Crossroads for Textile & Apparel Transformation appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: COVID-19 revealed a paradox in organizational life: even with half the mid-level workforce physically present and reduced office hours, many companies not only survived but thrived. This disruption exposed inefficiencies in traditional hierarchies – layers of reporting, redundant roles, and micromanagement – that often obstruct value creation rather than enable it. Instead of information crawling up and down multiple layers of hierarchy, Zoom meetings and digital platforms turned the pyramid into a network. Everyone could see the same dashboards, hear the same updates, and know their role directly. That eliminated the endless chain of “someone reports → someone approves → someone executes.” This is the method the company adopted at that time, which is called ‘heterarchy’. But unfortunately, most of the company went back to their old school; only a few carry some good habits. Photo: Nazmut Tarek, General Manager, Nahl Fashion Ltd What if we adopt “Heterarchy” in our industry? Conventional hierarchies offered accountability, control, and order. When the world was slower and smaller, it worked. For example, information was hard to get by, communication was delayed, organizations were spread out geographically, formal authority was needed to make decisions, and technology was limited. When the environment shifts, but the structure doesn’t, problems arise. The flow of information has been altered by digital technologies. Why do organizations still act as though they need to climb a ladder when knowledge is now instantly available? About 75 years ago, heterarchy was initially introduced in cybernetics by Blackmore. summary: Rising production costs, energy uncertainty, global competition and changing buyer expectations are putting new demands on Bangladesh’s ready-made garment industry. Meeting these challenges requires more than investment in machinery and technology. It also calls for stronger skills, practical knowledge and the ability to share and apply that knowledge across factory teams. Against this backdrop, Independent […] The post Independent Apparels partners with Panacea to strengthen skills for a changing RMG sector appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Rising production costs, energy uncertainty, global competition and changing buyer expectations are putting new demands on Bangladesh’s ready-made garment industry. Meeting these challenges requires more than investment in machinery and technology. It also calls for stronger skills, practical knowledge and the ability to share and apply that knowledge across factory teams. Against this backdrop, Independent Apparels Ltd. has partnered with Panacea Private Consulting Group on a two-year Manufacturing Excellence project. The initiative aims to improve factory performance while building the skills and internal capability needed to sustain improvements over time. The launch was attended by S. M. Abu Tayyab, Managing Director of Independent Apparels; Syed Tanzim Mozaher, Director, Independent Apparels Ltd; Brothers Apparels Ltd; and members of the company’s leadership team. Dr. Azim Mohammad, Managing Director of Panacea, joined the event with the firm’s Vice President, Senior Consultant, and other team members. Improving productivity depends on better work methods, informed decision-making and the ability to identify and solve problems at the factory level. These changes are more likely to last when employees understand new practices, can apply them in their work and share what they learn with colleagues. Knowledge and skills transfer will therefore be an important part of the project. Under the leadership of Mr. Tayyab, Independent Apparels is pursuing improvements across its manufacturing operations. Established in 1997, the company has a longstanding presence in Bangladesh’s apparel industry. title: If The Product Is Everything, Then Product Data Has To Be Everywhere
summary: A product promise is made up of images, a written description, and a set of attributes. Those elements define eCommerce today, and they are fundamental to a vision for agentic commerce that depends on that data being available and being true. The post If The Product Is Everything, Then Product Data Has To Be Everywhere appeared first on The Interline .
content: THE INTERLINE PODCAST · 52 MIN If The Product Is Everything, Then Product Data Has To Be Everywhere Listen to If The Product Is Everything, Then Product Data Has To Be Everywhere Follow the show Apple Podcasts Spotify Hey, welcome back to The Interline Podcast. We started a couple of shows this season already with a bit of a thought exercise, but hopefully you’ll humour me if we do it again. I want you to think about the last thing you bought online that wasn’t quite what you expected when it arrived. Maybe the colour was different in the daylight. Maybe the fabric was thinner than it looked in the photos. I’m sure they shipped you the right size, in the sense that you ordered a small and you got a small, but maybe that meant something different on your body to what it meant in the size guide. There’s a spectrum of outcomes that can spin off from those kinds of potential mismatches between the product promise and the product reality. On one end, it’s a minor thing. You’ll live with it, either because you decided it just wasn’t a big deal versus how much you like the product, or because the friction of returning it outweighed the impact of the issue. On the other, it’s a whole brand-loyalty-breaching crisis. Not only did the product go back, it went back with a stern note and a lot of anger around it, and it coloured all your future interactions with that company. The severity of the reaction you had is kind of beside the point, weirdly, because both of those extremes have the same root cause: the information you were given to make your buying decision on top of was either inaccurate or incomplete in some way. title: Government, factory owners and labour leaders unite to restore RMG stability
summary: Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury has urged readymade garment (RMG) workers to return to work from today (5 November), while calling on factory owners to reopen factories temporari...
content: Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury has urged readymade garment (RMG) workers to return to work from today (5 November), while calling on factory owners to reopen factories temporarily closed. Additionally, he assured government support and security to restore normal operations in the sector. Figure: Ariful Haque Choudhury, Minister, Labour and Employment The appeal came following a high-level tripartite meeting involving government representatives, garment factory owners and labour leaders at the Ministry of Labour and Employment amid ongoing wage-related unrest in key industrial areas. Speaking at a press conference after the meeting, the minister said the government would provide all necessary assistance to ensure a safe working environment and help resume normal production activities across the garment sector. Choudhury also expressed condolences over the death of a garment worker during the recent unrest and said local administration officials had visited the affected family following government directives. Addressing concerns over wage demands, the minister noted that the newly formed wage board had already held its first meeting within days of its formation. He said the government expects to complete the wage revision process in line with its plan to implement the new wage structure by December. Labour leaders representing organizations affiliated with BNP, Jamaat-e-Islami and the National Citizen Party (NCP) also called on workers to return to work and support efforts to normalize industrial operations. At the same time, they demanded the withdrawal of cases filed against workers and the release of those detained during recent demonstrations. content: By: Seshadri Ramkumar, Professor, Texas Tech University, USA (Lubbock, USA, November 04, 2026)— Creating new markets for cotton is a priority for the global cotton sector. Gen Z researchers endeavor to create new cotton products with advanced applications. Global cotton industry is working to enhance its market share by: 1) developing new products such as advanced textiles, 2) engaging with youth population, and 3) improving the quality-cost balance. United States-based Cotton Incorporated is engaged in research and development and marketing to increase the consumption of cotton. Recent research by two undergraduate students in the Nonwovens & Advanced Cotton Laboratory at Texas Tech University, USA utilized plasma surface modification to improve functional and mechanical properties of cotton nonwoven products. The students were from the Departments of Physics and Astronomy and Biology, emphasizing the need to have multidisciplinary approach in developing value-added cotton products. Research at the Nonwovens and Advanced Cotton Laboratory at Texas Tech University focuses on increasing the demand for cotton by developing advanced textiles from cotton and outreach to increase the utility of sustainable products. The laboratory engages with undergraduates and high schools and encourages them in undertaking research on cotton and sustainable materials for functional applications. Plasma treatment used Argon gas to develop stronger oil absorbent cotton nonwovens. Building on earlier research on the application of raw cotton as an absorbent for crude oil, undergraduate students focused on exploring additional functionalities. content: By K. Executive Director Mrs. Radhika Bhagwati discusses the company’s technological strengths, evolving customer requirements and plans for INDIA ITME 2026. InspirOn Engineering has steadily strengthened its position in textile finishing through its Motex range of stenter machines, combining engineering expertise with a focus on productivity, fabric quality and cost-effectiveness. The company’s journey in stenter manufacturing began in 1996 through a joint venture with A.Monforts, Germany. Since then, it has supplied more than 300 machines worldwide. Mrs. Radhika Bhagwati, Executive Director According to Mrs. Radhika Bhagwati, (ED), InspirOn Engineering, three priorities are increasingly shaping product development: sustainability, automation and flexibility. Textile processors require equipment that can handle diverse fabric types, deliver consistent quality and reduce energy consumption without compromising productivity. “Customers expect machines that save energy, handle diverse fabrics and deliver consistent quality , and that’s where Motex has evolved,” she says. Engineering for Productivity and Energy Efficiency A key differentiator of the Motex range is its patented Uniflo Air Circulation system, which delivers up to 15% higher drying efficiency at the same power consumption, according to the company. By integrating alternating segments of flexible polydimethylsiloxane and amino blocks into a single backbone, this unique architecture maximizes luxurious hand-feel while radically enhancing yellowing resistance and application stability. Unlike […] The post Plug-and-play silicone softener provides effortless textile finishing appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: The emergence of linear block silicone copolymers marked a major paradigm shift in textile finishing, overcoming the performance trade-offs inherent in conventional amino and amido-silicone softeners. By integrating alternating segments of flexible polydimethylsiloxane and amino blocks into a single backbone, this unique architecture maximizes luxurious hand-feel while radically enhancing yellowing resistance and application stability. Unlike traditional silicones that frequently fail under harsh processing conditions, the securely configured functional groups in block silicones withstand high shear, extreme pH, and elevated temperatures. Figure: Edward Menezes, Executive Chairman, Rossari Biotech Ltd. While most standard block copolymers effectively use high-shear homogenization or microemulsification to form oil-in-water emulsions stabilized by suitable surfactants, this approach carries some inherent practical and technical limitations. Process dependency: Achieving and maintaining a fine, stable emulsion particle size depends on emulsification equipment, surfactant selection, and careful process control, both at the manufacturer and, for in-house emulsified products, at the mill. Bath stability issues: Conventional emulsions can be sensitive to electrolytes, hardness, pH swings, and the presence of other anionic or cationic auxiliaries in the finishing bath, increasing the risk of creaming, flocculation, or silicone spotting on fabric. Shelf-life and logistics: Coarser or less robustly stabilized emulsions are more prone to phase separation during storage and transport, particularly across temperature fluctuations. content: By K. Gopalakrishnan Jintex’s Ganesh H.R. explains how A Team is combining Taiwanese machinery, chemistry, automation and process expertise to help Indian manufacturers accelerate their move into MMF, sportswear and technical textiles. India’s textile industry is entering a decisive new phase. The country has built formidable scale and capability in cotton, but the next wave of growth is increasingly being shaped by man-made fibres (MMF), functional textiles, sportswear, athleisure and technical applications. Recognising this shift, Jintex Corporation Ltd. has joined forces with a group of established Taiwanese machinery, automation and textile-technology companies to create A Team—an integrated platform designed to bring Taiwan’s synthetic-textile know-how closer to Indian manufacturers. In an interaction with The Textile Magazine, Ganesh H.R., Senior Vice President – South Asia, Jintex Corporation Ltd., explains why India’s synthetic-textile opportunity is gathering momentum, how A Team was conceived, and why technology must be supported by process knowledge, local service and application expertise if India is to compete successfully in global performance-textile markets. Ganesh H.R., Senior Vice President – South Asia, Jintex Corporation Ltd. India’s Synthetic Opportunity India’s shift towards synthetics has become far more visible over the past three to four years. Jintex had been tracking the segment for more than a decade, but Ganesh says the recent acceleration is materially different in both pace and intent. The structural reason is clear: while India remains strongly cotton-oriented, the global fibre mix is increasingly dominated by synthetics. summary: New textile finishing technologies introduced by Switzerland’s Sanitized and Germany’s Rudolf are designed to address two factors that can limit the useful life of clothing and technical textiles – persistent odours and declining weather protection. Sanitized has introduced Odorex EON, a biocide-free treatment developed to tackle the accumulation of body oils and odour-causing residues in […] The post Helping fabrics retain their functional properties appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: New textile finishing technologies introduced by Switzerland’s Sanitized and Germany’s Rudolf are designed to address two factors that can limit the useful life of clothing and technical textiles – persistent odours and declining weather protection. Sanitized has introduced Odorex EON, a biocide-free treatment developed to tackle the accumulation of body oils and odour-causing residues in performance apparel, while Rudolf has launched Ruco-Dry Eco CWS, a water-repellent finish designed to provide improved resistance to rain and moisture, particularly in cotton fabrics. The two companies are highlighting their respective developments as part of a broader approach to textile durability that extends beyond conventional measures such as strength, abrasion resistance and wash performance. One particular challenge for sportswear manufacturers is the persistence of unpleasant odours in synthetic garments, even after repeated laundering. Sometimes referred to as “permastink”, this can result from the gradual accumulation of sebum and other residues within textile fibres. Sanitized Odorex EON employs a dual-action approach intended to address both immediate odours and their longer-term accumulation. During wear, the treatment adsorbs and neutralises odour molecules, while also creating a protective layer that helps release sebum residues during laundering. The aim is to prevent the progressive build-up of contaminants that can make otherwise serviceable garments unpleasant to wear. summary: Techtextil and Texprocess will return to Frankfurt am Main from 4-7 April 2028 with a stronger focus on connecting materials, production technologies and textile processing. The two international trade fairs will introduce an optimised hall layout designed to encourage collaboration, improve visitor navigation and generate new business opportunities across the textile value chain. Against a […] The post Techtextil and Texprocess to boost industry connectivity appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Techtextil and Texprocess will return to Frankfurt am Main from 4-7 April 2028 with a stronger focus on connecting materials, production technologies and textile processing. The two international trade fairs will introduce an optimised hall layout designed to encourage collaboration, improve visitor navigation and generate new business opportunities across the textile value chain. Against a backdrop of volatile markets, rising costs and changing global supply chains, the events aim to help textile manufacturers, technology suppliers and end users identify new partnerships and applications. Developments in advanced materials, automation and artificial intelligence are creating opportunities for innovation, making closer cooperation between different stages of production increasingly important. Organiser Messe Frankfurt says the concurrent staging of Techtextil and Texprocess provides a significant advantage by bringing together research organisations, material suppliers, machinery manufacturers, processors and industrial users at a single location. The close relationship between the two events was evident in 2026, when 87% of Texprocess trade visitors also attended Techtextil, while 68% of Techtextil visitors explored Texprocess. Around 80% of exhibitors reported achieving their trade fair objectives. Several leading international companies have already confirmed their participation in the 2028 editions. Early registrations for Techtextil include Angles Textil/Antex, Beaulieu Fibres International, CHT, Dilo Systems, Getzner Textil, Huvis Corporation, Lenzing, Sioen Industries and Toray Textiles Europe. Meanwhile, Kornit, Veit and ZSK Stickmaschinen are among the first companies to commit to Texprocess, reflecting continued industry interest in technologies for processing

content: Santoni China Group will participate in ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 , taking place from November 20–24 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center (NECC) in Shanghai. Under the theme “Machines Evolved · Intelligence Delivered,” the Group will showcase circular and seamless knitting technologies, innovative textile applications, the SWS 3D AI design platform and integrated digital solutions from its brands, including Santoni, Jingmei and Terrot, at Hall 4.1, Booth C39 . Founded in Brescia, Italy, in 1919, Santoni has built a century-long legacy of innovation in knitting technology. Since establishing its manufacturing presence in China in 2005, Santoni China has remained at the forefront of the knitting industry, advancing both circular knitting machinery and the transformative potential of digitalization and artificial intelligence. Today, the Group brings together six distinctive equipment and component brands, four integrated engineering, R&D and manufacturing hubs, and a digital ecosystem designed for intelligent manufacturing. By uniting hardware with software, and specialist expertise with scalable capabilities, Santoni China Group goes beyond creating the machines and technologies that shape the fabrics of tomorrow—it is helping reimagine the future value chain of knitted products. title: New garment wage structure to take effect in December
summary: A revised wage structure for Bangladesh’s garment workers will come into effect in December, according to members of the newly formed wage board. Representatives of both employers and workers agreed...
content: A revised wage structure for Bangladesh’s garment workers will come into effect in December, according to members of the newly formed wage board. Representatives of both employers and workers agreed to the timeline during the board’s meeting on 4 November. The announcement comes amid ongoing protests in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur, where garment workers are demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from Tk 12,500 to Tk 30,000. Workers have also called for an end to alleged blacklisting practices and what they describe as unjust layoffs. The government formed a six-member wage board on 1 November to review the existing wage structure following widespread demonstrations and clashes between workers and law enforcement agencies. The board has begun discussions aimed at determining a revised minimum wage acceptable to both workers and employers. Meanwhile, protests continued on Monday as police dispersed demonstrators in Savar’s Hemayetpur area after they attempted to move towards the Dhaka-Aricha Highway. Law enforcement used tear gas to clear the protesters, who have been holding demonstrations for several consecutive days. The labour unrest has disrupted factory operations across several industrial zones, forcing hundreds of garment factories to temporarily suspend production and leading to road blockades in major manufacturing areas. Industry stakeholders hope the wage board’s decision and the planned implementation of a new wage structure in December will help ease tensions and restore stability to Bangladesh’s vital garment sector.

World cotton production is estimated at 25.75 million tonnes, down approximately 4% from 26.85 […] The post Consumption to Exceed Production Based on Resilient Demand in Asia appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Global cotton consumption is projected to exceed production in the 2026/27 season as output declines across several major producing countries while demand remains relatively stable, according to the November edition of Cotton This Month , published by the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC). World cotton production is estimated at 25.75 million tonnes, down approximately 4% from 26.85 million tonnes in 2025/26. Global consumption, meanwhile, is projected to increase slightly to 26.10 million tonnes, compared with 25.89 million tonnes the previous season. The projections indicate that consumption will exceed production by approximately 353,000 tonnes, reversing the previous season’s production surplus of nearly 961,000 tonnes. The shift suggests a modest drawdown in global cotton inventories. Production Declines Across Major Suppliers The decline in global production reflects reduced crop prospects in several major cotton-producing countries. China’s production is projected to fall by approximately 4%, from 7.5 million tonnes to 7.2 million tonnes, while Brazil’s output is expected to decline by about 2%, from 4.25 million tonnes to 4.10 million tonnes. Production in Pakistan is also forecast to fall by approximately 17%, while the United States is expected to record a decline of about 4%. India’s production is projected to remain stable at 5.3 million tonnes, while West African output is expected to increase modestly to approximately 954,000 tonnes. The outlook remains subject to weather-related risks, particularly in India and West Africa, where irregular rainfall, drought, excessive moisture, and pest pressure could affect yields and lead to further revisions as the season progresses. content: Three years after its launch in English, Spanish, French and Turkish, Barmag’s Digital Academy online training centre for the BCF process is now also available in Chinese. Available on the e-commerce platform myBarmag.com, it offers a wide range of e-learning modules on the operation, maintenance, and repair of the Neumag BCF S+ and S8 systems. The training programme is aimed at operators, process engineers and technicians, as well as quality managers. Compact, role-based learning units, accessible via mobile and desktop devices, allow users to quickly apply the content. At the same time, the programme consistently shares Barmag’s OEM expertise regarding the operation and maintenance of the machines. In contrast to work methods that have evolved individually, all processes are standardised and followed through in complete detail. This ensures that users learn and apply the defined best practices. Progress assessments help participants internalize the contents and reinforce what they have learned and exams and certificates document their learning achievements. Feedback features can quickly clarify comprehension questions at any time. Access to the Digital Academy is granted on a location or company-specific basis. Around 450 active users have already recognised the benefits of Barmag’s digital classroom for themselves. Most of them are based in the US but with the launch of the Chinese version, this service is now accessible to an even larger customer base. title: All About AI: Begüm Dogru Öztekin of Refabric
summary: Refabric's Co-founder & CEO on why trust in AI will be built from an underlying fashion data layer, practical results, and consistency over time. The post All About AI: Begüm Dogru Öztekin of Refabric appeared first on The Interline .
content: Originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , this executive interview with Refabric is one of a 17-part series that sees The Interline quiz executives from companies who have either introduced new AI solutions or added meaningful new AI capabilities into their existing platforms . For more exclusive interviews, stories and opinions from different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from voices from every level of fashion, download The AI Report 2026 . We’re observing a big disconnect (in both our own fashion-only data and in wider benchmarks from other sources) between the increasing capability and reliability of AI, in both a general sense and in discrete applications, and the lack of trust that end users place in its outputs. What does trust in your specific applications of AI look like, and how do you achieve and measure it? For us, trust is built on consistency. Every image is preprocessed, every prompt is enriched, and every request is routed through a pipeline built specifically for fashion use cases. Every ingested image is analyzed down to its finest fashion-specific attributes, construction details, fabric behavior, trim, and stitch. This is not a generic vision model with a fashion layer on top; the pipeline is built for fashion from the ground up. But we measure trust the way our customers do: in practical results. Fewer sampling rounds, fewer corrections, production-ready outcomes. We track exactly those metrics with our enterprise clients. When the output becomes reliable enough to act on without rework, trust follows naturally. Most AI tools that touch design and / or development start with one or more off-the-shelf, industry-agnostic models, and they primarily begin with quick-win visualisation and sharing as their targets. content: The UCC 672-ME combines electronic three-way needle selection on cylinder and dial with exceptional design flexibility, production efficiency and application-driven textile innovation. Terrot Textilmaschinen GmbH, the German circular knitting machinery manufacturer and a premium engineering provider within the Santoni China Group, will showcase its UCC 672-ME at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 in Shanghai, China. Designed for premium mattress ticking, upholstery and other demanding textile applications, the double electronic circular knitting machine combines independently programmable three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial with high production output and extensive patterning capabilities. The technology enables manufacturers to develop sophisticated, double-sided fabric structures while increasing design flexibility and supporting efficient, application-specific textile manufacturing. Dual-sided technology expands design possibilities At the heart of the UCC 672-ME is electronic three-way needle selection on both cylinder and dial. By independently programming knit, tuck and miss actions at every feeder on both needle systems, manufacturers can create intricate jacquard patterns, three-dimensional textures, ventilation zones and reversible fabric structures with extensive design freedom. At ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026, Terrot will highlight a 38-inch UCC 672-ME configured in E20 gauge with 88 feeders and electronic three-way selection on both needle systems. The exhibition machine features a specialized mattress-fabric concept combining differentiated fabric zones, comfort-oriented construction and ventilation structures on both fabric sides. summary: Embroidery machine manufacturer ZSK has introduced an open API and direct integration with Anthropic’s Claude AI platform to its MY.ZSK 4.0 monitoring system, allowing manufacturers to analyse production data and build their own performance dashboards without programming expertise. The development is intended to make the extensive operating data generated by industrial embroidery machines more accessible […] The post ZSK brings AI-powered production analysis to embroidery appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Embroidery machine manufacturer ZSK has introduced an open API and direct integration with Anthropic’s Claude AI platform to its MY.ZSK 4.0 monitoring system, allowing manufacturers to analyse production data and build their own performance dashboards without programming expertise. The development is intended to make the extensive operating data generated by industrial embroidery machines more accessible to production managers, enabling them to identify inefficiencies, investigate recurring problems and compare performance across machines, shifts and manufacturing sites. Every connected ZSK machine generates information on stitch counts, operating speeds, thread breaks, downtime, setup times and individual embroidery designs. While this information has previously been accessible through the company’s MY.ZSK monitoring portal, the new API allows it to be integrated into manufacturers’ own enterprise resource planning (ERP), manufacturing execution systems (MES) and other production management tools. Natural language The integration with Claude takes this a stage further by allowing users to interrogate the data through natural language commands rather than having to develop their own software. Production managers can, for example, ask which embroidery designs are responsible for the most thread breaks, how much production time is lost during colour changes or whether a particular order is likely to meet its delivery deadline. Claude can retrieve and analyse the relevant machine data and present the results as charts or complete web-based dashboards, incorporating key performance indicators, machine comparisons and production trends over periods of seven, 30 or 60 days. content: From November 20 to 24, 2026, the Trützschler Group will present its latest fiber processing technologies at ITMA Asia in Shanghai, China. Visitors are invited to meet our experts in Hall 5.1, Booth D20 and discover solutions designed to increase productivity, simplify operations and support greater efficiency across spinning preparation and nonwoven production. Key highlights include the automated can transport system T-CAN, the next-generation card TC 30, innovative card clothing solutions such as STEELTOP and SUPERFLOW, as well as advanced nonwoven technologies for hygiene, wipes and filtration applications. T-CAN is Trützschler’s automation solution designed to reduce labor dependency and support greater automation in spinning mills. Trützschler Spinning At ITMA Asia 2026, Trützschler Spinning will showcase technologies that help spinning mills increase productivity, improve operational efficiency and make better use of valuable raw materials. A key highlight will be T-CAN, Trützschler’s automated can transport system. Designed to reduce labor dependency and support greater automation in spinning mills, T-CAN automates sliver transport throughout spinning preparation. It connects cards and drawing passages while ensuring reliable material allocation. By reducing manual handling and supporting continuous production, the system helps lower labor requirements, minimize downtime and improve operational efficiency. Visitors will also have the opportunity to learn more about the next-generation card TC 30 . Customers achieve up to 40% higher productivity in man-made fiber applications while maintaining or even improving yarn quality. title: Georg Stausberg Takes Over As CEO Of The Rieter Group With Immediate Effect
summary: WINTERTHUR, Switzerland — November 4, 2026 — The Board of Directors of Rieter Holding Ltd. was confronted by the designated CEO, Daniel Lippuner, with additional demands regarding his compensation package, particularly his bonus. Due to irreconcilable differences, Daniel Lippuner will not assume the position. Georg Stausberg, CEO of Barmag, will assume the position of CEO […]
content: WINTERTHUR, Switzerland — November 4, 2026 — The Board of Directors of Rieter Holding Ltd. was confronted by the designated CEO, Daniel Lippuner, with additional demands regarding his compensation package, particularly his bonus. Due to irreconcilable differences, Daniel Lippuner will not assume the position. Georg Stausberg Georg Stausberg, CEO of Barmag, will assume the position of CEO of the Rieter Group with effect from November 4, 2026. Georg Stausberg has more than three decades of experience in the international textile machinery industry and has shaped the development of Barmag in various leadership positions. Under his leadership as CEO, Barmag consolidated its position as the world’s leading supplier in the man-made fiber sector. After Barmag was acquired by Rieter in February 2026, Georg Stausberg became a member of the Rieter Group’s Executive Committee. With his extensive industry expertise and his international network, Georg Stausberg is one of the most prominent leaders in the global textile machinery industry. Posted: November 4, 2026 Source: Rieter Holding Ltd.

summary: The growing importance of bio-based materials in performance apparel was a central theme at the latest Functional Fabric Fair in Portland, Oregon, which attracted record attendance and more than 350 exhibitors. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from October 26-28th, the event recorded a 7% increase in attendance compared with its autumn 2025 edition, with […] The post Bio-based materials take centre stage at record Portland fair appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The growing importance of bio-based materials in performance apparel was a central theme at the latest Functional Fabric Fair in Portland, Oregon, which attracted record attendance and more than 350 exhibitors. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from October 26-28th, the event recorded a 7% increase in attendance compared with its autumn 2025 edition, with a sold-out exhibition hall that included more than 50 companies participating for the first time. The exhibition, organised by Functional Fabric Fair powered by Performance Days, brought together textile suppliers, apparel manufacturers, designers and sourcing specialists to explore material developments for the autumn/winter 2027/28 season. A particular emphasis was placed on bio-based materials as the performance apparel industry seeks alternatives to fossil-derived fibres and finishes, while addressing increasingly demanding requirements for durability, functionality and environmental performance. The programme examined not only the potential of renewable raw materials, but also the practical challenges involved in bringing new technologies to commercial scale, including feedstock availability, traceability and certification. Cellulose Forum A new Cellulose Forum was introduced to highlight developments in natural and regenerated cellulosic fibres, ranging from hemp, flax and nettle to lyocell, modal and viscose. It joined established forums dedicated to cotton and wool, reflecting growing interest in the performance potential of natural and renewable materials. Other specialist areas explored advances in garment construction, finishing technologies and functional fabrics for sportswear, outdoor clothing, bodywear and workwear. On 27 August 2026, the country’s peak demand hit 19,027MW at 9PM. Replacing […] The post Energy-efficient fans could cut Bangladesh’s peak power demand by up to 2,590MW: IEEFA appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: A national programme backed by bulk procurement and carbon revenue could make the switch to energy-efficient BLDC fans affordable for low-income households Key takeaways Household fans for space cooling alone account for up to 5,212 megawatts (MW) of Bangladesh’s summer power demand. Yet energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) fans make up less than 2% of household fans. Replacing energy-inefficient household fans with BLDC fans could cut summer power demand by up to 2,590MW and avoid over USD4 billion in future investment in coal-fired plants. It could also save 6,913 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity a year, worth BDT89.87 billion (USD0.73 billion). Households lack information on the availability of BLDC fans and their energy-saving potential. In addition to raising awareness, the Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority (SREDA) should finalise standards and labels for fans to nudge consumers towards efficient models. The government could design a national programme to cut the upfront cost of BLDC fans through bulk procurement and recycle the programme’s carbon revenue to make them affordable for low-income households. Household fans add up to 5,212 megawatts (MW) to Bangladesh’s summer power demand, with usage peaking around 9PM. On 27 August 2026, the country’s peak demand hit 19,027MW at 9PM. Replacing energy-inefficient fans with the energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) models could cut peak demand by up to 2,590MW, according to a new report by the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA). title: Missoni streamlines collections with Lectra PLM
summary: Italian fashion house Missoni has strengthened its product development and collection management processes with Lectra’s Kubix Link product lifecycle management (PLM) platform, achieving a 60% reduction in time spent managing and maintaining product data. The cloud-based solution has enabled Missoni to centralise product information, improve collaboration between departments and suppliers, and support the integration of […] The post Missoni streamlines collections with Lectra PLM appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Italian fashion house Missoni has strengthened its product development and collection management processes with Lectra’s Kubix Link product lifecycle management (PLM) platform, achieving a 60% reduction in time spent managing and maintaining product data. The cloud-based solution has enabled Missoni to centralise product information, improve collaboration between departments and suppliers, and support the integration of its Missoni Home business into the company’s internal operations. Founded in 1953 by Ottavio and Rosita Missoni, the Italian luxury brand is internationally recognised for its distinctive knitwear, colourful geometric patterns and innovative textile designs. Its portfolio has expanded beyond fashion into sportswear, beachwear, accessories and home furnishings. The decision to bring Missoni Home operations in-house created new requirements for managing product development, production and supply chain information. The company needed a flexible digital platform capable of supporting multiple departments while integrating with existing business systems. Missoni selected Kubix Link, building on a relationship with Lectra that began more than 25 years ago with the introduction of computer-aided design (CAD) technology. The PLM platform provides a centralised environment for managing product specifications, technical documentation and collection data, allowing internal teams and external partners to access consistent information throughout the development process. Following an initial analysis phase, the implementation progressed to a live system after 12 months, beginning with the creation of master data for a new collection. title: Rising raw material costs and price competition pressure Taiwan textile manufacturers
summary: Taiwan's textile industry is expected to face continued weakness in its core operations through the end of 2026 as rising raw material costs and intense price competition put pressure on manufacturers...
content: Taiwan's textile industry is expected to face continued weakness in its core operations through the end of 2026 as rising raw material costs and intense price competition put pressure on manufacturers' profitability. Figure: Inflation and geopolitical tensions have changed international brands' ordering patterns.Courtesy: Collected Chemical fiber producers reported that domestic raw material prices have increased by more than 30% year-on-year. Further price increases in September made it difficult for manufacturers to adjust their selling prices quickly enough to recover higher production costs. Although some manufacturers increased product prices in the second half of the year, strong market competition limited their ability to pass on additional costs. Standard-grade products faced particular pressure because of intense price competition and limited profit margins. Manufacturers are also facing competition from producers in China and Southeast Asia, where lower-priced products are affecting the performance of Taiwan's textile companies. Meanwhile, inflation and geopolitical tensions have changed international brands' ordering patterns. Brands are increasingly moving away from long-term orders toward shorter-notice orders with tighter delivery schedules. This has made production planning more difficult for manufacturers. Hong Yi Fiber Industry Co., a long-established draw-textured yarn manufacturer, continues to generate around 30% of its product mix from standard-grade yarns. The company has been shifting toward higher-value products, including composite and specialty yarns. However, its textile operations remained unprofitable in the first half of 2026. title: Change at the top for Rieter
summary: Georg Stausberg has been appointed CEO of the Rieter Group with immediate effect after a dispute over remuneration resulted in the withdrawal of the company’s previously designated chief executive, Daniel Lippuner. In an unusually frank announcement on November 4th, the Swiss textile machinery group said its board of directors had been confronted with additional demands […] The post Change at the top for Rieter appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Georg Stausberg has been appointed CEO of the Rieter Group with immediate effect after a dispute over remuneration resulted in the withdrawal of the company’s previously designated chief executive, Daniel Lippuner. In an unusually frank announcement on November 4th, the Swiss textile machinery group said its board of directors had been confronted with additional demands from Lippuner concerning his compensation package, particularly his bonus arrangements. The company said the resulting differences had proved irreconcilable and that Lippuner would therefore not be taking up the position. Instead, Rieter has appointed Georg Stausberg, CEO of Barmag, to lead the group with effect from November 4th, 2026. Stausberg brings more than three decades of experience in the international textile machinery industry, having held a succession of senior management positions at Barmag, one of the world’s leading suppliers of machinery and systems for man-made fibre production. As CEO, he played a central role in strengthening Barmag’s position in the global synthetic fibre machinery market. Following Rieter’s acquisition of Barmag in February 2026, Stausberg joined the group’s executive committee, providing him with direct involvement in the enlarged organisation. His appointment now places an established industry figure at the head of Rieter as it continues to integrate Barmag into its operations and strengthen its position across the global textile machinery market. Rieter said Stausberg’s extensive industry expertise and international network made him one of the most prominent leaders in the sector. www.rieter.com The post Change at the top for Rieter appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

title_ko: Shantnu Nikhil의 John Jacobs x S&N: 인도 패션과 이탈리아 디자인의 만남
summary: Shantnu and Nikhil make their first-ever foray into eyewear with a collaboration with John Jacobs for a bold, fashion-forward collection, now available at Lenskart stores. Two distinct design worlds. One statement-making collaboration. John Jacobs joins forces with celebrated couturiers Shantnu and Nikhil’s pret label, S&N by Shantnu Nikhil, to launch a 32-piece eyewear collection that […] The post John Jacobs x S&N by Shantnu Nikhil: Indian Couture Meets Italian Design appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Shantnu and Nikhil make their first-ever foray into eyewear with a collaboration with John Jacobs for a bold, fashion-forward collection, now available at Lenskart stores. Two distinct design worlds. One statement-making collaboration. John Jacobs joins forces with celebrated couturiers Shantnu and Nikhil’s pret label, S&N by Shantnu Nikhil, to launch a 32-piece eyewear collection that marks the designers’ first-ever venture into eyewear. Bringing together John Jacobs’ Italian design sensibilities and S&N’s distinctive design language, the collection reimagines iconic eyewear through bold design, elevated detailing and a strong point of view. Inspired by The Shape of India , the collection draws from the spirit of influential Indian leaders whose eyewear became symbols of conviction, intellect and authority. Reinterpreted for a new generation, these timeless forms get a contemporary, fashion-forward edge. The details make the statement. From the iconic S&N mark on the curve of the frame to precision metal streak detailing across the temples, every element is designed to stand out. The finishing touch? S&N’s iconic navy blue and cherry-red tape accents, tucked into the folding hinges. Together, these signature details give the range a distinctive identity, bringing the unmistakable S&N aesthetic to eyewear. Spanning eyeglasses and sunglasses across wayfarers, aviators, round frames and bold square silhouettes, the collection explores rich colours, premium refined materials and statement-making shapes. Designed to move effortlessly from everyday dressing to occasion wear, these frames bring a new edge to festive outfits, wedding looks and everything in between. content: By K. Gopalakrishnan A legendary German circular knitting brand returns with renewed strength, a sharper customer focus and India at the heart of its global growth strategy Few names in circular knitting command the recognition, respect and technological credibility of Mayer & Cie. Founded in 1905, the German company has spent more than 120 years building a reputation around precision engineering, premium-quality circular knitting machines and technologies that have shaped generations of textile manufacturing. Over its history, the company has delivered more than 80,000 machines worldwide, establishing a formidable installed base and a brand synonymous with premium circular knitting. But even the strongest industrial brands can face extraordinary challenges. Mayer & Cie. entered insolvency proceedings in late 2025, bringing uncertainty to one of the world’s most respected names in circular knitting. What followed, however, has become an extraordinary revival story. In April 2026, the acquisition of the circular knitting machinery business by Xu Hongjie, from the family behind China’s Huixing Machinery, was formally completed, clearing the way for Mayer & Cie. Global to restart operations in Albstadt. For Xu Hongjie, the acquisition was not simply an opportunity to acquire an established machinery business. It was an opportunity to preserve a globally respected technology brand and build upon its strengths. “We are convinced of the unique value of the brand, the quality of the machines, and are deeply impressed by the technical expertise of the new team,” says Xu Hongjie. The significance of the revival lies precisely in what the new ownership has chosen not to change. Mayer & Cie. Global remains rooted in Albstadt. Design systems, product lifecycle management (PLM), enterprise resource planning (ERP), production planning, manufacturing execution systems (MES) and individual […] The post Linking the modern mill’s islands of data appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: While the textile industry has spent much of the past decade digitalising individual parts of its manufacturing chain, connecting them all together represents the next big challenge, according to the latest ITMA 2027 textile machinery exhibition blog. Design systems, product lifecycle management (PLM), enterprise resource planning (ERP), production planning, manufacturing execution systems (MES) and individual machines can all generate increasingly sophisticated data. Too often, however, it all remains trapped within separate systems. Few companies illustrate the potential of doing things differently as dramatically as Shein. The fashion giant’s rapid-response business model has been built around a highly digitalised supply chain connecting information on consumer demand with suppliers and manufacturing. “We reimagined the supply chain, which is a daunting task, and we’ve done it by digitising the small and medium-sized factories to give them visibility to see their own capacity, continued order flow and seamless efficiency,” Shein executive chairman Donald Tang has explained. Shein uses data analytics to test products in small initial batches and respond rapidly to actual demand, scaling production up or down accordingly. Whatever the wider debate surrounding the ultra-fast-fashion model, its approach demonstrates the competitive possibilities when information can move quickly between previously separate parts of the supply chain. Separate evolutions This principle is becoming increasingly relevant to textile manufacturers and not simply to meet demands for greater efficiency. summary: Bangladesh and South Korea have agreed to form a joint working group to increase investment, expand trade, and address business challenges. The decision follows the conclusion of negotiations on a Com...
content: Bangladesh and South Korea have agreed to form a joint working group to increase investment, expand trade, and address business challenges. The decision follows the conclusion of negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). Figure: Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance and Planning Minister, shakes hands with Jung-sung Park, South Korean Trade Minister, ahead of a bilateral meeting in Seoul today. Photo: Ministry of Finance The working group will include government agencies and business chambers from both countries. It will identify investment opportunities and support joint projects through public-private partnerships (PPPs). The decision came at a meeting between Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, Finance and Planning Minister, and Jung-sung Park, South Korean Trade Minister, in Seoul on November 3, 2026. Bangladesh wants to expand its traditional textile and garment partnership with South Korea. The two countries also see opportunities in power and energy, renewable energy, electronics, semiconductors, shipbuilding and advanced manufacturing. For Bangladesh's textile and apparel industry, cooperation could bring new investment in textile technology, modern machinery and energy solutions. Renewable energy is also an important area as factories seek reliable power and lower energy costs. Bangladesh highlighted several steps to improve its investment climate. These include reducing customs duties on electronics raw materials from 26% to zero, automating capital repatriation and simplifying customs and port procedures.
