summary: The European Commission has imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of PET spunbond nonwovens originating in China, a decision welcomed by European industry association EDANA. The measures, published on October 30th, 2026, follow the introduction of provisional duties on May 12th. Effective from October 31st for a period of five years, the definitive duties range […] The post EU gets tough on nonwovens dumping appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: The European Commission has imposed definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of PET spunbond nonwovens originating in China, a decision welcomed by European industry association EDANA. The measures, published on October 30th, 2026, follow the introduction of provisional duties on May 12th. Effective from October 31st for a period of five years, the definitive duties range from 39.8% to 48.1%. The Commission’s investigation concluded that Chinese imports had increased significantly during the period examined and were being sold at unfairly low prices, causing substantial harm to the EU PET spunbond industry. It also determined that the introduction of anti-dumping measures was in the wider interests of the European Union. The duties are intended to restore fair competition and safeguard European production capacity. “We welcome the Commission’s decision to impose definitive anti-dumping measures,” said Jacques Prigneaux, market analysis and economic affairs director at EDANA. “The adoption of definitive anti-dumping duties sends an important signal that the Commission is determined to effectively address unfair trade practices on the EU market. “Restoring fair competition is essential not only for safeguarding EU production, but also for supporting the investments in innovation, sustainability and employment that are required to meet the EU’s strategic industrial ambitions.” EDANA said it would continue working with EU and national customs authorities to monitor the implementation of the measures and ensure their effective application. The association also welcomed the Commission’s investigation and its commitment to maintaining fair market conditions within the European Union. www.edana.org The post EU gets tough on nonwovens dumping appeared first on Innovation in Tex

title: Bangladesh eyes global manufacturing hub status through regional production networks
summary: Bangladesh aims to become a global manufacturing hub and export gateway by developing integrated production networks across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa. Courtesy: Ban...
content: Bangladesh aims to become a global manufacturing hub and export gateway by developing integrated production networks across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa. Courtesy: Bangladesh High Comission Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Adviser to the Prime Minister on finance and planning, outlined the ambition at the inaugural session of the 29th Sustainable Development Conference in Islamabad, Pakistan, on November 2. He proposed a regional manufacturing network and said cooperation between Bangladesh and Pakistan could establish a new model of economic partnership. He also emphasized attracting investment that strengthens domestic industrial capacity, transfers technology, and creates jobs. The ambition comes as Bangladesh seeks to diversify its export base. According to Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) data, the country earned $48 billion from merchandise exports in FY2025-26. Readymade garment exports contributed $38.70 billion, accounting for approximately 80.6% of total exports. This dependence highlights the need to expand other manufacturing sectors, including leather goods, footwear, light engineering and pharmaceuticals. A World Bank-supported export diversification project has already demonstrated the employment potential of non-RMG industries, helping nearly 180,000 people secure jobs in targeted export-oriented firms. During the Pakistan visit, Haroon Akhtar Khan, Pakistan's adviser on industries and production, identified solar technology, battery manufacturing and electric vehicles as potential areas for bilateral cooperation. Discussions also covered technology transfer, joint ventures and industrial investment. title_ko: Fakir Technologies는 FKL Spinning Mills에서 6.13MWp 태양광 프로젝트 계약을 체결했습니다.
summary: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agre...
content: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh, the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually. For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh's solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies' commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj, in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. content: US-based polymer specialist Americhem has acquired Noble Biomaterials, the developer of antimicrobial and conductive technologies for textiles and other soft surface applications. The acquisition brings Noble’s specialist technologies into Americhem’s global operations, strengthening the ability to support customers from initial product development through to commercial-scale production. Noble supplies proprietary materials technologies for applications in apparel, textiles, healthcare, aerospace and defence. Its established Ionic+, X-Static and Circuitex platforms provide antimicrobial, odour control and electrical conductivity functions, supported by US manufacturing operations and an extensive intellectual property portfolio developed over more than two decades. The acquisition will strengthen Americhem’s position in functional fibres and polymer solutions, particularly in healthcare and other markets requiring advanced material performance. “This is an exciting step forward for Americhem as we continue to invest in high-growth, high-demand markets,” said Americhem CEO John Richard. “Noble Biomaterials brings exceptional capabilities in antimicrobial solutions, strong commercial relationships and a reputation for quality that aligns with our values.” The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. www.americhem.com www.noblebiomaterials.com The post Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

title_ko: Trident는 ₹4,650 crore 확장 드라이브로 앞서 나가고 있습니다.
summary: Trident Limited has approved a ₹4,650-crore expansion and modernisation programme across its yarn, sheeting, paper and renewable energy businesses. Cleared by the board on November 2, 2026, the projects are… The post Trident powers ahead with ₹4,650-crore expansion drive appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Trident Limited has approved a ₹4,650-crore expansion and modernisation programme across its yarn, sheeting, paper and renewable energy businesses. Cleared by the board on November 2, 2026, the projects are scheduled for completion in stages between December 2027 and September 2029, with funding through internal accruals and debt. Mr. Rajinder Gupta, Chairman, Trident Group The largest investment, ₹1,660 crore, will go towards a new yarn manufacturing facility at Dhar, Madhya Pradesh, with a capacity of 1,99,680 spindles. Trident has already acquired 179.2 acres of leasehold land for the project at an approximate cost of ₹106.09 crore. The facility is expected to be completed by September 30, 2029. At its existing yarn facility in Budhni, Madhya Pradesh, the company will invest ₹1,022 crore in expansion and modernisation, targeted for completion by December 31, 2027. The programme includes the addition of 99,840 spindles, replacement of 48,000 older spindles with 70,176 new spindles for finer-count yarns, and replacement of 960 older rotors with 2,400 new rotors. Trident’s existing yarn operations across Sanghera, Punjab, and Budhni have 7,46,064 spindles, 5,424 rotors and 320 air-jets. Capacity utilisation at Budhni stands at 94%. The sheeting business will receive ₹1,018 crore for the addition of 336 looms, taking its loom capacity from 504 to 840. Scheduled for completion by January 31, 2028, the expansion comes against reported capacity utilisation of 58%. In paper, Trident plans to invest ₹296 crore to add 28 tonnes per day, increasing manufacturing capacity from 479 to 507 tonnes per day. title: Car Seat, Structures and Interior Component Supplier Brose Sitech Selects Richland County, S.C. For First US Manufacturing Facility
summary: COLUMBIA, S.C. — October 28, 2026 — Brose Sitech, a supplier of car seats, structures and interior components, today announced it selects Richland County for its first U.S. manufacturing facility. The company’s $29.5 million investment will create 330 new jobs. Brose Sitech develops and produces complete seats, structures and other seat components. With its global […]
content: COLUMBIA, S.C. — October 28, 2026 — Brose Sitech, a supplier of car seats, structures and interior components, today announced it selects Richland County for its first U.S. manufacturing facility. The company’s $29.5 million investment will create 330 new jobs. Brose Sitech develops and produces complete seats, structures and other seat components. With its global headquarters in Poland, the company has 22 locations internationally, including its regional headquarters office in Detroit. Located at the Just in Time facility in the Scout Supplier Park in Blythewood, Brose Sitech’s new 140,000-square-foot facility will supply the new Scout Motors plant with complete car seat sets. Operations are expected to be online in 2027. Individuals interested in joining the Brose Sitech team should visit the company’s careers page. “Establishing our first manufacturing location in Blythewood is an important milestone for Brose Sitech. The U.S. is a significant automotive market with strong opportunities for future growth. With our new production facility, we are bringing our expertise in complete seating systems closer to our customer Scout while laying the foundation for Brose Sitech’s long-term development in North America.” -Brose Sitech Columbia Inc. Executive Vice President Juan-Carlos Kieler “With the addition of 330 new jobs in the Palmetto State, we are proud to welcome Brose Sitech to Richland County. By joining Scout Motors’ Supplier Park, the company is building on South Carolina’s position as a leader in automotive manufacturing and helping create new opportunities for our people.” -Gov. content: TEMPE, Ariz. — November 2, 2026 — Economic activity in the manufacturing sector expanded in October for the 10th consecutive month, say the nation’s supply executives in the latest ISM ® Manufacturing PMI ® Report. The report was issued today by Susan Spence, MBA, Chair of the Institute for Supply Management ® (ISM ® ) Manufacturing Business Survey Committee. “The Manufacturing PMI ® registered 55.5 percent in October, 1 percentage point above the September figure of 54.5 percent. The overall economy expanded for the 24th month in a row. (A Manufacturing PMI ® above 47.5 percent, over a period of time, generally indicates an expansion of the overall economy.) The New Orders Index expanded for the 10th consecutive month after four straight readings in contraction, registering 55.5 percent, up 0.2 percentage point compared to September’s figure of 55.3 percent. The October reading of the Production Index (59 percent) is 2.3 percentage points higher than the 56.7 percent recorded in September and the highest since November 2021 (60.5 percent). The Prices Index remained in expansion (or ‘increasing’ territory), registering 75.2 percent, a 2.7-percentage point decrease compared to September’s reading of 77.9 percent. The Backlog of Orders Index registered 54.6 percent, down 1.8 percentage points compared to the 56.4 percent recorded in September. The Employment Index reading of 52.4 percent is down 0.3 percentage point from September’s figure of 52.7 percent,” says Spence. “The Supplier Deliveries Index indicated slowing performance for the 11th month in a row after one month in ‘faster’ territory. Organised by AVK, the German Federation of Reinforced Plastics, the annual awards recognise advances in composite […] The post Three innovations recognised at AVK Composites Awards appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Three developments in lightweight construction, automated manufacturing and advanced fibre reinforcement have taken first places in the three categories of the 2026 AVK Innovation Awards, presented at the JEC Composites Talks DACH held in Cologne, Germany, on October 20th. Organised by AVK, the German Federation of Reinforced Plastics, the annual awards recognise advances in composite products, manufacturing processes and scientific research. Products and applications Dresden-based Anybrid secured first place in the products and applications category for a heavy-duty diamond core drill incorporating a carbon fibre-reinforced thermoplastic body in place of conventional steel. Developed with partners including Avanco Composites, Mitsui Chemicals Europe, AFPT, Hilti Kunststofftechnik and TU Dresden, the component has combined laser-based tape winding with injection moulding to produce a lightweight structure with integrated metal connections. The resulting drill assembly achieves a weight reduction of approximately 70% compared with steel, at least doubles service life and reduces its carbon footprint by around 37%. The development has successfully completed mechanical testing and practical field trials. Processes and manufacturing CompriseTec won the processes and methods category for a robotic manufacturing technology that eliminates the need for conventional moulds when producing thermoplastic composite components. Developed with the Hamburg University of Technology’s Institute of Aircraft Production Technology and Invent, the process employs two cooperating robots to shape heated, continuous fibre-reinforced thermoplastic sheets into complex geometries. content: At ITMA ASIA 2026, KARL MAYER will demonstrate its expertise in processing staple fibers during warp preparation and will return to where this technology belongs: the Weaving Hall, at Booth 3/A24. The focus here will be on the latest-generation WARPDIRECT direct warping machine, featuring various yarn tensioners, as well as the sophisticated HSB Size Box – the centerpiece of the innovative PROSIZE sizing machine. Figure 1: The WARPDIRECT Both technologies are aimed specifically at manufacturers of high-quality goods in the commodity sector. "Our machines produce warp beams of the highest quality with high process efficiency. This offers particular advantages to textile manufacturers who are focused on generating real added value in a highly competitive market," says Enzo Paoli, President of the Warp Preparation Business Unit at KARL MAYER. WARPDIRECT: With the highest speed to precision warp beams Since its launch at the end of last year, the WARPDIRECT 2.0 has already been successfully deployed worldwide. Its performance is particularly valued in India, but also in China and Europe. Its strengths include identical warping lengths for all warp beams and high production output. In practice, warping speeds of up to 1,200 m/min are achieved. Figure 2: Enzo Paoli , President of the Warp Preparation Business Unit at KARL MAYER In addition, the current machine version stands out thanks to an upgrade to the press roll system. The change from hydraulic to electric operation reduces maintenance requirements while ensuring precise warping quality. In combination with an optimal yarn depositing device, this results in completely cylindrical beams with precise yarn arrangement. summary: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) has proposed harmonized end-of-waste (EoW) criteria for textile, textile-related and footwear waste to support reuse and remanufacturing across th...
content: The European Commission's Joint Research Centre (JRC) has proposed harmonized end-of-waste (EoW) criteria for textile, textile-related and footwear waste to support reuse and remanufacturing across the European Union. The technical report, published on 26 October 2026, aims to reduce regulatory differences among member states and establish common conditions for recovered textiles to re-enter the market as products rather than waste. Figure: Under the revised Waste Framework Directive, Member States must establish separate collection systems for used textiles from 2025. Courtesy: Collected The proposal addresses a regulatory gap in Europe's circular textile value chain. Currently, differences in national waste classifications create uncertainty for waste-management operators, textile sorters, reuse platforms, remanufacturers and downstream buyers. A harmonized framework could make it easier for businesses to handle recovered materials and trade reusable textile products across national borders. The European Environment Agency (EEA) estimated that the EU generated 6.95 million tons of textile waste in 2020, equivalent to around 16 kg per person. Of this amount, 82% came from post-consumer textiles, including used clothing and household textiles. Around 11.6 kg per person ended up in mixed household waste, while only 4.4 kg was collected separately for reuse and recycling. The challenge extends beyond waste collection. According to the EU's revised Waste Framework Directive, less than 1% of clothing waste is currently used to produce new clothing through textile-to-textile recycling. content: Building on its extensive screen and hybrid printing expertise, SNQS International is advancing from Kornit Atlas MAX PLUS to India’s first Kornit Apollo, supported by a flexible business model designed for scalable digital growth. Since its founding in 1990, SNQS International has been part of Tiruppur’s textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem for more than three decades. Established by V. Elangovan, a textile engineer and industry visionary, SNQS has grown into an end-to-end apparel supply chain partner serving international retail and brand customers. Krishna Elangovan, Director at SNQS International As founder and Managing Director of SNQS International, Elangovan continues to guide the company’s development and long-term vision. He also serves as Vice President of the Tiruppur Exporters’ Association, reflecting his contribution to the wider advancement of Tiruppur’s export industry. Under his leadership, SNQS has developed extensive manufacturing capabilities, including more than two decades of experience in conventional screen and hybrid printing. Responding to Changing Brand Expectations While conventional screen printing remains effective for long, repeatable production runs, global fashion and apparel requirements are evolving. Brands increasingly expect shorter product-development cycles, faster sampling, flexible order quantities, rapid replenishment, and greater design variety. They also need manufacturing partners that can respond more precisely to actual consumer demand while reducing inventory exposure, overproduction, and waste. content: CLEARWATER, Fla.— November 3, 2026 — PCP Ventures LLC, a Florida-based investor group, announced that it completed the acquisition of Pellon on October 1. Pellon is a globally recognized textile brand that makes specialty materials used in everything from clothing and quilts to home décor and crafts. Pellon’s products help give finished items shape, support, softness and cushioning, and include interfacings, stabilizers, batting, fiberfill, foams and other specialty fabrics. The company, which employs approximately 95 people, produces its products at a 220,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Clearwater, Florida. Pellon has been a globally trusted name among sewists and quilters for decades, so much so that “Pellon” is widely used as the generic term for interfacing. The brand’s products are often described as the “Magic in the Middle” characterized as the hidden yet essential materials inside a project that provide the support, structure, and functionality needed to bring the finished product together. Under PCP Ventures, Pellon will continue providing products for do-it-yourself sewing enthusiasts through stores such as Walmart, Hobby Lobby and Michael’s. The company sees tremendous potential in expanding its reach to users in other industries. The market is vast, given that Pellon’s products can be used in apparel, quality, sewing, furniture and a wide range of consumer applications. Leadership Committed to the Brand PCP Ventures is led by a Florida-based investment group representing family offices with combined assets of close to $1 billion, including Adam Schoenbaum and Ron Ciganek. content: CARY, N.C. — November 3, 2026 — FiltXPO 2026 brought together filtration industry leaders, manufacturers, researchers, product developers and technology innovators Oct. 28-29 at the Minneapolis Convention Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Organized by INDA, the Association of the Nonwoven Fabrics Industry, FiltXPO provided a forum for industry professionals to discover innovative filtration technologies, explore emerging market opportunities, exchange technical expertise and build business relationships. The two-day event featured an exhibition showcasing filtration products, materials, components and manufacturing technologies, and the Advances in Filtration Technical Conference, which addressed the trends and challenges shaping the future of air, gas, water and liquid filtration. FiltXPO 2026 Innovation Award Winners Announced A highlight of the event was the presentation of the FiltXPO 2026 Innovation Awards, recognizing advancements in filtration technology, performance and sustainability. The winners were honored in two categories: Air/Gas Filtration Innovation Award Solberg Manufacturing Inc. — Fully Automated Liquid Management System Imagine giving a vacuum system the ability to continuously manage heavy liquid loads with less operator involvement. title: BAPEX discovers 97.69 BCF gas well in Noakhali
summary: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX) has discovered an estimated 97.69 BCF of natural gas at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well in Noakhali’s Companiganj. The di...
content: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX) has discovered an estimated 97.69 BCF of natural gas at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well in Noakhali’s Companiganj. The discovery is expected to strengthen local energy security and support efforts to reduce dependence on imported fuels. Courtesy: Collected The discovery was confirmed on 2 November through a gas flare test after drilling operations at the well in Rampur Union were completed. According to BAPEX, the estimated gas reserves are spread across two zones of the well. The gas is valued at approximately Tk 5,809 crore at consumer-level prices, while the well is expected to supply 15 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid. Gas extraction from the well is expected to continue for the next 20 years. Drilling at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well began on 8 July this year using BAPEX's Bijoy-10 rig. The operation reached a depth of 3,289 meters and was financed jointly by the government and BAPEX. The Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources undertook the drilling initiative based on the findings of BAPEX's three-dimensional (3D) seismic survey. Mohammad Mozammel Haque, Project Director of the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well, confirmed the discovery. He said further observation and a Drill Stem Test (DST) over the next 15 days would determine whether oil or any other substance is also present in the well. The discovery comes as Bangladesh continues to explore domestic gas resources to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imported fuels.

summary: Bangladesh needs around $2 billion (Tk 25,000 crore) in investment, along with skilled manpower and stronger infrastructure, to achieve its 4,000MW rooftop solar target within a year. Figure: Banglad...
content: Bangladesh needs around $2 billion (Tk 25,000 crore) in investment, along with skilled manpower and stronger infrastructure, to achieve its 4,000MW rooftop solar target within a year. Figure: Bangladesh needs $2bn investment to achieve 4,000mw rooftop solar target. Courtesy: Collected The observations were shared during a discussion titled “Rooftop Solar: Is Adding 4,000MW in a Year Viable?” held at The Daily Star Centre in Dhaka. Energy experts say the ambitious goal is achievable, but success will depend on financing, policy support, grid upgrades, and rapid capacity building. Despite acknowledging the challenges, experts agreed that the target is achievable if bureaucratic obstacles are removed and financing mechanisms are strengthened. However, they emphasized that success will depend not only on installing solar panels but also on developing a skilled workforce, upgrading the electricity grid and ensuring long-term maintenance. Dipal C Barua, Founder and Chairman of Bright Green Energy Foundation, stressed the need to prioritize decentralized renewable energy alongside conventional power generation. He argued that Bangladesh's reliance on imported fuel could be reduced by encouraging households, businesses and farmers to generate electricity through rooftop solar, small wind turbines and biogas systems. Barua said both conventional power and solar energy could have developed simultaneously over the years, helping the country avoid recurring power shortages and load-shedding. He also highlighted opportunities in solar irrigation and agrivoltaics and called for stronger quality control measures to ensure consumer confidence in renewable technologies. content: Dhaka, 3 November 2026: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project , in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh , the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO ₂ emissions annually . For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh’s solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies’ commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj , in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from 26-28 October, the event attracted its highest attendance to date, up 7% compared with […] The post Functional Fabric Fair reaches new heights appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Functional Fabric Fair powered by Performance Days has reported record attendance at its Fall 2026 edition in Portland, reinforcing its growing importance as an international sourcing and innovation platform for the performance textiles industry. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from 26-28 October, the event attracted its highest attendance to date, up 7% compared with Fall 2025. The exhibition hall sold out with more than 350 exhibitors, while the opening OIA Catalyst Conference also reached capacity, bringing together more than 300 industry professionals. The results reflect the increasing significance of Functional Fabric Fair and its partnership with Performance Days, which together provide an expanding international platform connecting textile manufacturers, technology developers, apparel brands and sourcing professionals. With an established presence in Europe through Performance Days in Munich and a growing programme of Functional Fabric Fair events across the United States, the partnership is strengthening its position as a year-round meeting point for the global functional textiles industry. As the show continues to grow, it has become an even more effective platform for expanding our network and supporting our long-term growth The Portland exhibition attracted product developers, designers, sourcing specialists and senior executives from leading international brands, including Adidas, Arc’teryx, Columbia Sportswear, HOKA, Lululemon, New Balance, Nike, Patagonia, Under Armour and Vuori. A merchandiser opens an email from a buyer: “Can you confirm the shipment date?” Outside, workers are gathering. Inside, management is deciding whether production can continue safely. content: When the Factory Stops, Everyone’s Clock Keeps Running Imagine a factory on a November morning. Fabric is ready. Some garments are waiting for their final inspection. A merchandiser opens an email from a buyer: “Can you confirm the shipment date?” Outside, workers are gathering. Inside, management is deciding whether production can continue safely. The shipment clock is still running. So is the worker’s rent. So is the factory’s interest bill Figure: Ruhul Talukder, Managing Director, Ruhrose.com That is what makes Bangladesh’s current garment crisis so difficult. People standing on different sides of the factory gate are worried about the same thing: their future. The challenge is finding a way forward that they can trust. Behind the headlines are two kinds of pressure: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Their protests also include concerns about blacklisting and the reinstatement of dismissed workers. Reports of road blockades, clashes and attacks on property show how serious the situation has become. For workers, the discussion starts with daily life: food, rent, transport and the cost of supporting a family. For factory owners, it starts with a different calculation: the price agreed with the buyer, the cost of materials, wages, energy and the money left after shipment. Neither calculation disappears because the other side is struggling. A worker cannot pay rent with an explanation about low margins. A factory cannot meet a higher wage bill simply by wishing buyers would pay more. This is where leadership matters. The industry needs a workable agreement that recognises both realities. summary: In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF), discusses the material innovations and commercial decisions behind Taiwan’s drive to recover more value… The post Taiwan’s Textile Ambition: Making Responsibility a Competitive Advantage appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF), discusses the material innovations and commercial decisions behind Taiwan’s drive to recover more value from textile waste. By Nithin Kumar A performance fabric earns its reputation through what it does for the wearer. For Justin Huang, its value increasingly extends to what happens after use: whether its materials can be recovered and made useful again. Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF) Speaking exclusively to The Textile Magazine at the 30th Taipei Innovative Textile Application Show, TITAS 2026, Huang argues that material recovery can strengthen Taiwan’s position with global brands. With relatively high labour and energy costs, he says, Taiwanese suppliers must give international customers compelling reasons to choose them. He points to years of investment in materials and manufacturing processes intended to reduce environmental impact. In his account, taking responsibility for textile waste is becoming part of the value Taiwan offers its customers. Giving textiles another life A central priority is the move beyond PET-bottle recycling towards textile-to-textile recycling. Bringing discarded fabrics and garments back into fibre production would allow the industry to recover more of the materials contained in its own products. The difficulty begins with composition. Garments commonly combine different fibres, complicating the recovery process. Materials must be identified and sorted, while dyes and other unwanted substances may need to be removed. title: Techtextil And Texprocess 2028 Strengthen Networking And Business Opportunities Along The Textile Value Chain
title_ko: Techtextil 및 Texprocess 2028, 섬유 가치 사슬을 따라 네트워킹 및 비즈니스 기회 강화
summary: FRANKFURT AM MAIN, Germany — November 3, 2026 — Techtextil and Texprocess 2028 bring relevant market players even closer together. The focus is on the interfaces between materials, technology and processing – where innovations, new applications and business contacts emerge. The optimised hall layout supports this networking across the exhibition grounds, with short distances and […]
content: FRANKFURT AM MAIN, Germany — November 3, 2026 — Techtextil and Texprocess 2028 bring relevant market players even closer together. The focus is on the interfaces between materials, technology and processing – where innovations, new applications and business contacts emerge. The optimised hall layout supports this networking across the exhibition grounds, with short distances and an efficient route along the various stages of textile production and processing. Companies can register at early-booking rates until the end of November. The first renowned exhibitors have already registered. Techtextil-Texprocess 2026 Photo: Messe Frankfurt / Pietro Sutera Volatile markets, cost pressures and changing supply chains are challenging the global textile industry. At the same time, material innovations and new technologies such as AI are opening up additional applications and business opportunities. Collaboration along the value chain is essential. Techtextil and Texprocess bring together relevant market players in Frankfurt from 4 to 7 April 2028 who are shaping this transformation – from research and technology providers to manufacturers and processors as well as users from a wide range of industries. A major benefit lies in running the two leading trade fairs concurrently: together, they cover key production and processing stages at a single location, giving exhibitors access to new partners and fields of application beyond their own markets. Visitor behaviour also shows how closely the potential of the two events is intertwined: in 2026, 87 percent of Texprocess trade visitors also attended Techtextil. summary: 효성이 제주에서 인공증식한 멸종위기곤충 물장군 40개체를 자연에 방사했다. 지난해 비단벌레 방사에 이은 생물다양성 보전 활동으로, 임직원이 생태계 복원에 참여하는 기회를 확대하고 있다.효성은 지난 10월 29~30일 제주특별자치도 서귀포시 성산읍 일대에서 물장군 방사 행사를 진행했다. 행사에는 ㈜효성과 효성티앤씨, 효성중공업, 효성화학 등 4개 계열사 임직원이 참여했다.물장군은 연못과 습지에 서식하는 대형 수서곤충으로 습지 생태계의 상위 포식자다. 습지 감소와 농약 사용에 따른 수질오염 등으로 서식지와 개체 수가 줄어 멸종위기 야생

title: US trade show returns to Dhaka with $5 billion investment target
summary: The United States is seeking to expand its business and investment engagement with Bangladesh as the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) prepares to host the 30th US Trade Show in Dhak...
content: The United States is seeking to expand its business and investment engagement with Bangladesh as the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) prepares to host the 30th US Trade Show in Dhaka from November 5 to 7. The event comes as both countries look to strengthen trade relations, attract new investment and expand cooperation in technology, energy and manufacturing. The American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh holds a special press conference ahead of the ‘30th US Trade Show 2026’ at the Hotel InterContinental in the capital on November 2. | The three-day exhibition will take place at Hotel InterContinental Dhaka after a gap of two and a half years. It will showcase American products, services and technologies while providing a platform for business networking and investment discussions. AmCham announced the event at a press conference on November 2. According to the organizers, 43 exhibitors, including 36 companies and seven startups, will participate through 63 booths. Syed Mohammad Kamal, President, AmCham, said the chamber had previously set a target of attracting $5 billion in US investment to Bangladesh over the next five years. He emphasized that energy security would be essential to achieving this goal. "If this exhibition helps bring 10 to 12 new American companies to Bangladesh, that itself will be a major achievement," he said. The investment target comes against a backdrop of expanding bilateral economic relations. According to the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), total US-Bangladesh goods and services trade reached an estimated $13.7 billion in 2025, increasing 10.3% from 2024. title: Wage protests disrupt operations at over 300 garment factories
summary: Garment manufacturing operations faced disruptions across major industrial zones in Gazipur, Ashulia and Mirpur on Tuesday as workers continued demonstrations demanding higher wages. More than 300 fac...
content: Garment manufacturing operations faced disruptions across major industrial zones in Gazipur, Ashulia and Mirpur on Tuesday as workers continued demonstrations demanding higher wages. More than 300 factories announced temporary holidays or experienced production stoppages amid the ongoing situation. Courtesy: Collected According to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), 161 factories in Gazipur declared general holidays, while production remained suspended at 93 factories in the Savar, Ashulia and Zirani areas. Another 52 factories were also reported closed following work stoppages by workers. In Gazipur, demonstrations took place at several industrial locations, including Naojor, Bhogra, Palli Bidyut and Chandra. Workers attempted to block sections of the Dhaka-Tangail Highway, affecting traffic movement between Joydebpur Chowrasta and Naojor. Additional law enforcement personnel were deployed to manage the situation and maintain traffic flow. Similar disruptions were reported in Ashulia, where workers gathered at several points along the Baipail-Abdullahpur road. Although many workers initially joined their regular shifts, some factories subsequently suspended operations as a precautionary measure amid concerns over possible disruptions. The situation also affected industrial activity in Mirpur, where workers staged demonstrations in the Mirpur 11 area. Police and other security personnel were deployed in the affected locations to maintain order and facilitate a return to normal activities. In Gazipur, members of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) were also deployed alongside police to support security operations. Ned is familiar with Nonwovenn having spent six years as a non-executive director between 2016 […]
content: BRIDGWATER, England— November 3, 2026 — Ned Dorbin has been announced as Chief Executive Officer of Nonwovenn and of Technical Materials Group (TMG), as the combined businesses look to accelerate growth, working towards ambitious targets over the next few years. Ned is familiar with Nonwovenn having spent six years as a non-executive director between 2016 and 2022. He has 19 years of experience as a private equity investor, supporting the growth of businesses across a wide range of sectors with funding and strategic board input. Ned Dorbin Nonwovenn and TMG plan to significantly increase their scale over the coming years through a combination of organic growth and acquisitions. As CEO, Ned will be responsible for leading the businesses through this next phase, providing strategic direction and driving commercial performance. His experience of working with management teams, supporting investment decisions and scaling businesses will be central to delivering these ambitions. Former CEO Andrew Brownlow remains an important part of the leadership team, with an increased focus on strategic projects, capital investment programmes and operational development. Ned Dorbin, Chief Executive Officer at Nonwovenn and Technical Materials Group, said: “I’m delighted to be joining Nonwovenn and TMG. Having previously worked with Nonwovenn, I know how well positioned the business is to expand and capitalise on the opportunities ahead. content: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the opening ceremony of Bangladesh Solar Expo-2026 in the city this morning as the chief guest. The inaugural ceremony began at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in the capital, said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony. The Power Division and the Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL) jointly organised the expo for the first time with the theme “Utilise Every Inch of Rooftop, Increase Income through Solar Power”. Chaired by Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku, it was also joined by State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit, Finance Secretary Dr Md Khairuzzaman Mozumder and Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrukh. Ministers, state ministers, members of parliament, secretaries and senior government officials from different ministries also attended the programme. summary: Karl Mayer has further developed its TM Weft warp knitting machine for fashion and apparel applications, introducing a finer E 36 gauge, greater patterning flexibility and improved yarn tension control. The developments will be demonstrated at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, alongside a new collection of warp knitted fabrics designed to reproduce […] The post Extending warp knitting into finer fashion fabrics appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Karl Mayer has further developed its TM Weft warp knitting machine for fashion and apparel applications, introducing a finer E 36 gauge, greater patterning flexibility and improved yarn tension control. The developments will be demonstrated at ITMA Asia 2026 in Shanghai from November 20-24, alongside a new collection of warp knitted fabrics designed to reproduce the appearance of woven textiles while retaining the production and performance advantages of warp knitting. The company’s WovenLike concept combines the appearance and texture of woven fabrics with the flexibility, wrinkle resistance and ease of care associated with warp knitted constructions. It also offers opportunities for more efficient production, particularly when processing challenging materials such as linen, acetate and decorative effect yarns. The latest developments to the TM Weft include an E 36 gauge option for producing finer fabrics and a new EL pattern drive, allowing greater flexibility and speed in pattern development. Yarn tension is now continuously regulated rather than controlled through the previous system, simplifying operation and supporting more consistent fabric quality. The first comprises dense, textured constructions intended for autumn and winter apparel. Alongside the exhibitions, the DELTA Award for Architecture and Delta Festival of Architecture will be held. content: GREENSBORO, N.C.— October 29, 2026 — Unifi, Inc., the makers of REPREVE ® and one of the world’s leading innovators in recycled and synthetic yarns, today released operating results for the first fiscal quarter ended September 27, 2026. Highlights Net sales were $127.9 million, a decrease of 5.7% from the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Revenues from REPREVE Fiber products were $36.4 million and represented 29% of net sales, compared to $39.3 million or 29% of net sales for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Gross profit was $12.5 million and gross margin was 9.8%, compared to gross profit of $3.4 million and gross margin of 2.5% for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. SG&A expenses were $11.5 million, a decrease of 4.1% from the first quarter of fiscal 2026, primarily driven by cost reduction efforts. Net loss was $2.0 million, or $0.11 per share, compared to a net loss of $11.4 million, or $0.62 per share, for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Adjusted EBITDA* was $6.1 million, compared to a loss of $(2.5) million for the first quarter of fiscal 2026. Cash provided by operating activities was $3.7 million during the first quarter of fiscal 2027, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of positive cash generation. Debt principal was $90.9 million and Net Debt* was $64.8 million at September 27, 2026. Continued efforts across innovation and traceability through the introductions of CofiraTM, a versatile dual function yarn, Resist2OTM Pro, an advanced water-resistant yarn, and YarnProofTM, supporting compliance with yarn-forward requirements in North and Central America. summary: Nipaş Tekstil upgraded its Rieter cards C 80 with Carding Gap Control (CGC) to improve sliver quality and increase productivity. The modernization enables the mill to operate with consistently high… The post Rieter Carding Gap Control helps Nipaş Tekstil Enhance Sliver Quality appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Nipaş Tekstil upgraded its Rieter cards C 80 with Carding Gap Control (CGC) to improve sliver quality and increase productivity. The modernization enables the mill to operate with consistently high quality at higher production speeds while reducing maintenance efforts. Fig. 1: Carding Gap Control automatically maintains the optimal carding gap under all conditions Fig. 3: Watch the video to find out more about Nipas Tekstil’s experience with CGC Carding lays the foundation for a stable, efficient spinning process and a high-quality end product. A key parameter in achieving this is the carding gap – the distance between the flats and the cylinder – which directly affects both quality and performance. Carding Gap Control (CGC) automatically maintains the optimal gap under changing operating conditions, ensuring that the full potential of the 40 active flats is utilized. The contact-free system continuously monitors the distance between needle tips and cylinder clothing and adjusts the flat setting as required (Fig. 1). Improved quality with CGC Fig. 2: Ring-spinning manager Ömer Mutlu highlights how the Carding Gap Control is benefitting Nipaş Tekstil The benefits are clearly reflected in daily production. Ömer Mutlu, Ring Spinning Mill Manager at Nipaş Tekstil in Türkiye, states: “The modernization of the cards C 80 with CGC has significantly improved yarn quality.” He also highlights that the automatic control of the flat settings enables consistently high sliver quality while supporting higher production speeds (Fig. 2). title: What Should A Fashion AI Lead Actually Do?
summary: Selecting and implementing technology has never been the hardest part of transformation, and AI is no different. A set of hard-learned guidelines for today’s AI leaders. The post What Should A Fashion AI Lead Actually Do? appeared first on The Interline .
content: This article was originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 . Including profiles and exclusive interviews with 17 AI companies, stories and opinions from 12 different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from around 100 voices from every level of fashion, bottled and analysed, The AI Report 2026 is essential reading for anyone interested in AI for fashion. I’ve seen a lot of AI Lead job descriptions in the past 6 months, and they all ask for the same things: a deep technical background, experience in data science or IT transformation, and fluency across multiple tech stacks. They are, in other words, technology roles. That feels wrong to me. I held exactly this kind of role at G-Star RAW for close to three years, and when I look at those job descriptions now, I notice what’s missing more than what’s there. I know, first-hand, that the hardest parts of leading AI in a fashion organisation have almost nothing to do with technology. In this article, I want to explain what those missing pieces are, what I think it looks like to solve them, and how you can apply some of what I learned to your own AI strategies and transformations. Piece 1: don’t underestimate the friction built into what seems like a straightforward vision for the future. When we launched Maia, an AI-powered back-office employee at G-Star, the original problem we’d set out to solve was straightforward, well-scoped, and it had a clear value return. Our employee support teams, covering corporate and retail across multiple offices and languages, were being overwhelmed with support tickets. Hundreds of questions, often the same requests repeated for different people, in different languages, across different time zones. It was unsustainable and it was slowing down operations. title: US apparel import tariffs rise to 24.56% as AAFA calls for policy certainty
summary: The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has urged the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to address foreign trade barriers and provide greater certainty in US tarif...
content: The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has urged the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to address foreign trade barriers and provide greater certainty in US tariff policies. They warn that rising duties and regulatory restrictions are increasing costs for apparel, footwear, and travel goods companies. Figure:Total US tariffs collected on apparel, footwear, and travel goods reached $28.44 billion in 2025, up 68% from $16.89 billion in 2024. In its October 29 submission to the USTR's 2027 National Trade Estimate (NTE) Report on Foreign Trade Barriers, AAFA identified trade-related challenges across 12 countries, including China, India, Japan, Indonesia, Mexico, and Canada. The association said tariffs, customs procedures, technical standards, and import restrictions are disrupting supply chains and limiting market access. Rising tariffs increase industry costs According to data prepared by Trade Partnership Worldwide, LLC, the average trade-weighted tariff rate on US apparel imports increased from 14.70% in 2024 to 24.56% in 2025. Footwear tariffs rose from 12.26% to 23.75%, while travel goods tariffs increased from 13.85% to 22.83%. Total US tariffs collected on apparel, footwear, and travel goods reached $28.44 billion in 2025, up 68% from $16.89 billion in 2024. Through August 2026, the industry had paid another $17.90 billion, including $8.23 billion in additional duties imposed under presidential trade authorities. AAFA said overlapping tariffs under Sections 301, 232, 122, and 338 are making sourcing and long-term planning more difficult. It called for preventing multiple tariffs from applying to the same products, removing duties on manufacturing inputs and machinery, and providing sufficient notice before introducing new measures.

title: VistaPrint triples apparel production speed
title_ko: VistaPrint는 의류 생산 속도를 3배로 향상시킵니다.
summary: VistaPrint has increased its digital garment printing capacity by approximately 25,000 units per week following the installation of a Kornit Digital Apollo system, which is delivering production speeds around three times faster than its previous process. The investment is enabling the print and design company to reduce production turnaround times to approximately a day, while […] The post VistaPrint triples apparel production speed appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: VistaPrint has increased its digital garment printing capacity by approximately 25,000 units per week following the installation of a Kornit Digital Apollo system, which is delivering production speeds around three times faster than its previous process. The investment is enabling the print and design company to reduce production turnaround times to approximately a day, while improving operational efficiency and lowering production costs. Serving millions of small and medium-sized businesses across Europe, the United States, Canada and Australia, VistaPrint has expanded well beyond its original business card printing activities to offer a wide range of customised products, including apparel, promotional materials, packaging and signage. The company has worked with Israel-headquartered Kornit Digital since 2007, progressively upgrading its digital garment printing operations through successive generations of technology, including the Kornit Atlas and Atlas MAX systems. The latest investment in Apollo represents a further step towards high-volume, on-demand apparel manufacturing, allowing VistaPrint to respond more quickly to incoming orders while reducing the handling and labour requirements associated with garment production. The installation was supported by online training ahead of commissioning and an on-site Kornit technician during the first six months of operation. VistaPrint reached full utilisation across three production shifts approximately three months after production began. www.kornit.com www.vistaprint.com The post VistaPrint triples apparel production speed appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

The new AirOne loom has been developed specifically for this segment and features a newly designed crank shedding motion, combining high productivity with low […] The post Picanol enters basic fabrics market appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Picanol will introduce a new generation of airjet weaving machines at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai from November 20–24th, extending its portfolio into the market for basic woven fabrics. The new AirOne loom has been developed specifically for this segment and features a newly designed crank shedding motion, combining high productivity with low energy consumption, advanced digital capabilities and ease of operation. The launch follows extensive market research, R&D and field testing, and represents an important expansion of Picanol’s airjet weaving portfolio. AirOne will complement the established OmniPlus-i Connect, providing mills producing basic fabrics with an alternative designed around their specific production requirements. The machine incorporates a range of Picanol’s existing innovations and patented technologies, with particular emphasis on operational efficiency, sustainability and simplified machine control. “AirOne represents a special launch for Picanol,” says Johan Verstraete, vice president of weaving machines at Picanol. “This new machine platform brings together all the strengths that define Picanol today, from high performance and low energy consumption to digital capabilities and ease of operation. At the same time, it empowers us to enter a new market segment.” He adds that the company’s sales and service teams are looking forward to making Picanol technology accessible to a broader range of weaving mills. At the Shanghai exhibition, Picanol will demonstrate three machines on its stand F01 in Hall 3. The new AirOne will be producing poplin fabric, alongside an OmniPlus-i Connect weaving ladieswear fabrics and a Supermax rapier weaving machine producing denim. Technologies such as AI, automation, data analytics, and smart manufacturing are reshaping traditional production systems and creating new opportunities. To explore how these technological advancements are transforming the future of RMG manufacturing, we spoke with Zeeshan R. Khan, CTO of SurroundApps Inc. Below is a brief discussion for our respected readers. Photo: Zeeshan Khan, CTO, SurroundApps Inc. Textile Focus: How is sustainability developing in Bangladesh’s RMG sector? content: AI-powered automation, digital integration and flexible spinning technology to take center stage October 2026, Italy: Savio will showcase its latest advancements in winding and spinning technology at ITMA ASIA Shanghai 2026, highlighting the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI), automation and digital integration in textile manufacturing. The company will focus on two flagship machines: Proxima Smartconer®, its next-generation winding platform, and Lybra Smartspinner®, a versatile air-jet spinning solution. The innovations are designed to help textile manufacturers improve productivity, optimize energy consumption, enhance yarn quality and reduce processing costs while supporting more flexible and data-driven production. Proxima Smartconer®: Intelligent Winding for Higher Performance Savio’s Proxima Smartconer® is available in a comprehensive range of configurations, including fully automatic, manual feeding, cone-to-cone, Duo Lot and large bobbin feeding for the carded wool sector. The platform combines energy-saving technologies, optimized bobbin flow and AI-powered functions with Savio Insight, a web-based system for real-time production monitoring and control. Savio Insight enables remote machine setup, data tracking and performance analysis, helping manufacturers make informed decisions and improve winding process management. Another key innovation is a newly designed and patented suction nozzle in the preparation area. The component improves yarn-end capture efficiency while reducing energy consumption, contributing to lower operating costs without compromising reliability and quality. Held from 27-29 October 2026 at the Palais des Festivals in Cannes, the exhibition brought together leading European manufacturers of fabrics […] The post MarediModa Cannes signals renewed confidence appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: The 24th edition of MarediModa Cannes closed on an encouraging note, with renewed confidence among European textile manufacturers and international buyers, alongside the introduction of new creative formats and trend directions for Spring/Summer 2028. Held from 27-29 October 2026 at the Palais des Festivals in Cannes, the exhibition brought together leading European manufacturers of fabrics and accessories for beachwear, underwear and athleisure. More than 100 collections for Summer 2028 were presented, offering buyers an overview of developments in textile design, material innovation and performance. Despite continuing geopolitical and economic uncertainty, MarediModa reported results in line with the previous year, with no decline in overall activity. Organisers highlighted a more focused approach among visiting buyers, with greater attention to collection development, material selection and planning for future seasons. Claudio Taiana, President of MarediModa, said the results suggested a gradual return to confidence following a period of stagnation. “We had expected this edition to mark an acceleration after a period of stagnation linked to the international geopolitical situation. The figures are consistent with a return to programming and planning, reflected in more considered choices, closer examination of collections and a positive, vibrant atmosphere,” he said. Taiana also emphasised the exhibition’s role in promoting European textile manufacturing, particularly its combination of technical expertise, product quality and creative development. © MarediModa A significant addition to this year’s event was the inaugural Cannes Fashion Show, a new presentation format designed to demonstrate the creative and technological potential of fabrics through finished garments

content: The latest developments in hosiery technology, sustainable materials and artificial intelligence took centre stage at Legwear Innovation Day 2026, held last week at the Fulgar Event Space in Castel Goffredo, Italy. Organised by The Lycra Company in collaboration with Fulgar, the annual event brought together nearly 150 representatives from leading hosiery companies to explore market developments, emerging technologies and the fashion trends expected to shape the 2027/2028 season. The event reinforced the importance of collaboration and innovation within Italy’s historic hosiery manufacturing district, combining technical presentations with an immersive fashion performance showcasing new legwear concepts. Opening the programme, Ettore Manfrotto, Account Manager Brand & Retail at The Lycra Company, welcomed delegates before Alice Sperindio, EMEA Legwear Sales Manager, outlined the company’s activities across Italy and Europe. She highlighted opportunities to strengthen collaboration throughout the hosiery supply chain and support the development of new products and markets. Daniela Antunes, Marketing Manager at Fulgar, focused on the growing potential of bio-based textile technologies, presenting developments from Fulgar and The Lycra Company designed to reduce reliance on fossil-derived raw materials without compromising performance. © Fulgar These included EVO by Fulgar, a 100% bio-based yarn produced from renewable raw materials, comprising equal proportions of castor oil and industrial corn not intended for human consumption. The castor oil is sourced from crops grown in arid regions that do not compete with food production. content: Garment industry leaders met Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday, 2 November, to discuss the ongoing labour unrest and its impact on factory operations and exports. The meeting was held at the Ministry of Home Affairs at the Secretariat in Dhaka. Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin, Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, garment industry representatives and senior law enforcement officials, including Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, attended the meeting. The discussion comes amid continued protests by garment workers demanding a higher minimum wage. The unrest has disrupted production in several industrial areas and raised concerns over factory operations, shipment schedules and export performance. content: Bangladesh RMG Industry: Navigating Challenges and Securing Future Growth Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) industry stands at a pivotal moment. Escalating production costs, energy supply constraints, downward pricing pressure, global trade uncertainty, and the forthcoming graduation from Least Developed Country (LDC) status are collectively challenging the sector’s long-term competitiveness. Black,blue, grey and white t-shirts on hangers on gray background The path forward is not simply about producing larger volumes at lower prices. Sustained growth will require a strategic shift toward operational efficiency, productivity improvement, value-added products, stronger backward integration, and deeper collaboration between manufacturers and global retailers. The Role of International Buyers Building a resilient and sustainable apparel supply chain is a shared responsibility. To support long-term industry growth, international buyers should: • Provide greater visibility through reliable order forecasts and capacity commitments. • Avoid excessive price pressures that compromise sustainable manufacturing practices. • Participate in funding significant product, technology, and sustainability innovations where appropriate. • Engage suppliers earlier in product development, sourcing, and planning processes. • Recognize and reward measurable improvements in quality, productivity, compliance, and environmental performance. Stronger buyer-supplier partnerships will enhance both commercial outcomes and supply chain resilience. content: Groz-Beckert will present a broad portfolio of textile machinery components, precision tools and digital services at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026, taking place from 20-24 November in Shanghai, China. The German manufacturer will showcase innovations across knitting, weaving, nonwovens, sewing, tufting and spinning in Hall 4.1, Booth D41. Energy efficiency, process reliability and solutions for increasingly demanding textile applications will be central themes, with developments targeting technical textiles, medical products, fine-gauge fabrics and high-performance industrial materials. Knitting In circular knitting, Groz-Beckert will highlight its LCmax energy-saving needles, featuring a wave-shaped shank geometry designed to reduce friction and energy consumption while maintaining knitting performance and ease of handling. © Groz-Beckert For flat knitting, the company will introduce two special-application needles. The SAN TT has been developed for producing particularly tight loops, making it suitable for technical and medical textiles, while the new SAN FY is designed to process uneven effect yarns without compromising fabric appearance. A collaboration with Chinese company Sinotex will demonstrate fine-gauge knitting capabilities through a jointly developed knitted collar. content: Stronger industry-academia collaboration is essential to overcome mounting operational challenges in the ready-made garment (RMG) sector of Bangladesh. Rising worker wages and energy price instability currently threaten factory operations across the country. Academic figures and corporate leaders shared these insights at a panel discussion titled "Prospects and Challenges of the RMG Sector of Bangladesh" on November 1, 2026. The Department of Textile Engineering at Green University of Bangladesh (GUB) organized the event as part of TEX-FEST 2026 at its Purbachal American City campus. Figure: Academic figures and corporate leaders shared these insights at a panel discussion titled "Prospects and Challenges of RMG Sector of Bangladesh" on November 1, 2026. The garment sector serves as the primary driver of Bangladesh's national economy. However, unaligned policies and economic pressures put continuous stress on manufacturers. Prof. Dr. Mohammad Shorif Uddin, Vice-Chancellor, Green University of Bangladesh attended the program as the chief guest. He emphasized deeper partnerships between academic institutions and apparel manufacturers to drive industrial productivity. Economic instability creates massive operational hurdles for local factories. Prof. Dr. Khawza Iftekhar Uddin Ahmed, Pro-Vice-Chancellor, Green University of Bangladesh compared the RMG sector to a golden goose supporting the national economy. He warned that rising operational expenses, energy supply disruptions, and policy misalignment could severely damage the industry. He called for immediate university-industry synergy to protect the long-term sustainability of the sector. Severe energy supply shortages directly impact industrial production output. title: Gartex Texprocess expands to Eastern India with the launch of Kolkata edition in January 2027
summary: Building on nearly a decade of industry engagement and successful editions in Delhi and Mumbai, Gartex Texprocess India is set to expand its footprint to Eastern India with the launch… The post Gartex Texprocess expands to Eastern India with the launch of Kolkata edition in January 2027 appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
content: Building on nearly a decade of industry engagement and successful editions in Delhi and Mumbai, Gartex Texprocess India is set to expand its footprint to Eastern India with the launch of its Kolkata edition from 22–24 January 2027 at Biswa Bangla Mela Prangan, Kolkata. Organised by Messe Frankfurt Trade Fairs India Pvt Ltd and MEX Exhibitions Pvt Ltd, the Kolkata edition marks the next phase in the show’s growth journey, taking its established platform for textile and garment manufacturing to a region deeply rooted in India’s textile heritage and increasingly positioned for future manufacturing growth. West Bengal has long held a distinctive place in India’s textile landscape, with its rich handloom traditions, jute industry and established hosiery and garment manufacturing base. The state’s renowned weaving and craft clusters, including Fulia, Santipur, Bishnupur and Murshidabad, reflect a textile heritage that continues to shape the region’s identity. Kolkata and its surrounding districts are also regarded as the historical home of India’s hosiery industry, with a cluster that has grown over more than a century. The city is also a major centre for ethnic wear, kidswear, zari and embroidery work, while the Hooghly belt remains the heartland of India’s jute industry, now moving into bags, home textiles, geotextiles and composites. As the garment sector grows, so does the need for woven fabric, and the state has been encouraging powerloom and processing investment, among them the integrated textile park at Ashoknagar–Banipur. At the same time, manufacturers across Eastern India are increasingly looking towards modernisation, advanced machinery, technology adoption, capacity expansion and wider market access. title: Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow held in Hong Kong
summary: Bangladesh’s apparel industry took centre stage in Hong Kong on 28 October, as the Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow 2026 brought together around 130+ global buyers, sourcing professionals and industry leaders to showcase Bangladesh’s manufacturing capabilities and explore opportunities for growth. Co-hosted by BGMEA and HSBC, in collaboration with the Consulate General of the People’s Republic of […] The post Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow held in Hong Kong appeared first on Textile Focus .
content: Bangladesh’s apparel industry took centre stage in Hong Kong on 28 October, as the Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow 2026 brought together around 130+ global buyers, sourcing professionals and industry leaders to showcase Bangladesh’s manufacturing capabilities and explore opportunities for growth. Co-hosted by BGMEA and HSBC, in collaboration with the Consulate General of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh in Hong Kong, the event showcased Bangladesh’s manufacturing strengths, growing capabilities and ambitions for the future. A live apparel apparel showcase was among the highlights, bringing the quality, creativity and craftsmanship of Made in Bangladesh to life. The event featured opening remarks from Mahmud Hasan Khan, President of BGMEA, Oliver Jones, HSBC Hong Kong’s Head of Global Network Banking, Corporate and Institutional Banking, and Dr Shah Mohammad Tanvir Monsur, Consul General of Bangladesh in Hong Kong. Dr Rubana Huq, Chairperson of Mohammadi Group, delivered the keynote address, followed by panel discussions led by Md Mahbub ur Rahman, CEO of HSBC Bangladesh, featuring Ranjan Mahtani, Founder and Chairman of Epic Group, Sunny Malhotra, Managing Director of PDS Group, Dr Henry Soo, Managing Director of DataDevelop Consulting, Kim Hellström of H&M and Surendar Singh of Kontoor Brands. Discussions explored Bangladesh’s competitive positioning, evolving global sourcing priorities, product diversification, sustainability and the opportunities to move further up the value chain. The strong participation and exchange of perspectives reaffirmed the importance of collaboration between industry stakeholders in strengthening Bangladesh’s position in global apparel supply chains. The Legwear product group presents its exceptionally durable dur needles for use in sock and fine hosiery machines, where the highest levels of precision and load resistance are required. In the Warp Knitting segment, Groz-Beckert presents the patented compound needle Spec. 51/43.36 G 101 for fine-gauge elastic fabrics. The reinforced plastic part provides enhanced stability, while minimal tolerances support the production of uniform, high-quality fabrics with excellent knitting performance. title: ZDHC finds strong chemical data tracking, but weaker supplier follow-up
summary: The number of fashion and textile brands achieving the highest level of sustainable chemical management under the Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals (ZDHC) program increased to 21 in 2026 from 15 i...
content: The number of fashion and textile brands achieving the highest level of sustainable chemical management under the Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals (ZDHC) program increased to 21 in 2026 from 15 in the previous assessment. However, the latest report shows that brands still need to do more to help suppliers solve chemical management problems. Figure: The ZDHC Gateway provides factory-level information on chemical inventory conformance and wastewater performance.Courtesy: Collected The 2026 Brands to Zero Report, independently assessed by KPMG Netherlands, examines how brands manage chemicals through company policies, purchasing practices and supply chains. The program classifies brands into three levels: Pioneer, Accelerator and Champion. More brands collect and monitor chemical data The report shows that more brands are asking their suppliers to provide chemical inventory data. The share requiring suppliers to submit ZDHC InCheck data increased from 75% to 91%. The share of brands monitoring this data also rose from 87% to 91%. ZDHC InCheck helps factories check the chemicals in their inventories against the Manufacturing Restricted Substances List (MRSL). The list sets requirements for chemical formulations used in textile, leather and footwear manufacturing. However, collecting and checking data does not always lead to action. Only 74% of brands follow up with suppliers on the findings, although this figure increased from 60% in the previous assessment. This means that some brands identify chemical management problems but do not consistently follow up to ensure that suppliers address them. title: Fluoro-alternative finish from Dow
title_ko: Dow의 불소 대체 마감재
summary: Dow has launched a new silicone-organic hybrid textile finishing technology designed to provide durable water repellency alongside resistance to oil-based contaminants, without relying on conventional fluorinated chemistry. The new Dowsil IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion has been developed to help textile manufacturers and brands respond to increasingly stringent restrictions on fluorinated substances, while maintaining the performance, comfort […] The post Fluoro-alternative finish from Dow appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: Dow has launched a new silicone-organic hybrid textile finishing technology designed to provide durable water repellency alongside resistance to oil-based contaminants, without relying on conventional fluorinated chemistry. The new Dowsil IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion has been developed to help textile manufacturers and brands respond to increasingly stringent restrictions on fluorinated substances, while maintaining the performance, comfort and appearance of finished fabrics. Achieving effective oil repellency has traditionally been one of the major challenges in developing alternatives to fluorinated textile finishes. Dow says its third-generation silicone-organic hybrid technology is designed to address this limitation, offering resistance to both water-based stains and a range of oil-based contaminants. The product is intended for use on natural, synthetic and blended fabrics, although performance must be validated for individual fabric types and finishing formulations. The new emulsion can help protect against contaminants including cooking oils, motor oil and sebum, as well as common water-based stains such as coffee, wine and milk. “For years, achieving meaningful oil repellency in textiles typically required fluorinated chemistries, which are now facing increasing restrictions,” said Juan Carlos Medina, global strategic marketing director at Dow. “Dowsil IE-5619 helps close that gap with a silicone-based, fluoro-alternative solution that delivers durable water and oil repellency while preserving the softness, breathability and aesthetics consumers expect.” The new formulation is a 30% solids concentrate designed for integration into conventional textile finishing processes. content: China and India are among the world’s most important textile manufacturing markets and have been key destinations for Swiss textile machinery for decades. Their industrial structures, raw material bases and market dynamics, however, differ considerably. These differences create distinct requirements and opportunities for Swiss suppliers of machinery, components and services. With ITMA Asia + CITME in Shanghai and India ITME in Greater Noida, two major Asian textile machinery exhibitions will take place towards the end of 2026. “China and India are both key markets for our industry, but their industrial environments differ notably,” explains Cornelia Buchwalder, secretary general of Swiss Textile Machinery. “The structure of textile production, the availability of raw materials and the importance of domestic demand all influence their investment priorities. Understanding these differences is essential for our member companies to offer technologies that meet the specific requirements of each market.” Extensive value chain China is by far the world’s largest textile manufacturing country, with an extensive and highly integrated value chain covering virtually every stage of textile production. It is also the world’s leading exporter of textiles and apparel, while its substantial domestic market generates significant additional demand. Its position in man-made fibres is particularly strong, with chemical fibre production reaching approximately 87 million tons in 2025. At the same time, China remains a major cotton producer and processor. Exports continue to play a central role in the Chinese textile industry. Chinese textile machinery manufacturers have also made considerable technological progress, creating an increasingly competitive environment for international suppliers
